Remarks: Pure LiFePO4 (no Mn) -- background/mechanistic study on hydrothermal crystal growth via anion coordination polyhedron model + molecular simulation, NOT composition-specific LMFP data. No electrochemical or capacity data reported (purely computational/crystallographic). Key finding: growth rate order V{011}>V{210}>V{002}>V{101}>V{200}~=V{020}; dominant exposed facets under hydrothermal conditions are {020},{200},{101}. pH controls growth-unit speciation: plate-like crystals (large ac-plane facet) form at 4<pH<6.5, needle-like crystals at pH~=3.5, consistent with Dokko & Kanamura's prior experimental work cited in the paper.

Paper_Title: Nano-sized cathode material LiMn0.5Fe0.5PO4/C synthesized via improved sol-gel routine and its magnetic and electrochemical properties
Source_PDF: Advanced Energy Materials - 2012 - von Hagen - Electrospun LiFe1 yMnyPO4 C Nanofiber Composites as Self‐Supporting Cathodes.pdf
Synthesis_Method: High-energy ball-milling assisted sol-gel route: raw materials dissolved separately in 100 mL deionized water at molar ratio 2:1:1:2:2, manganese acetate mixed with citric acid, then FeCl2 and NH4H2PO4 added dropwise, LiOH.H2O added slowly with magnetic stirring at 80 C until a yellowish-brown wet gel forms; gel vacuum-dried >12 h, high-energy ball-milled, sintered 350 C 5 h in flowing argon, cooled slowly, ball-milled again and calcined 700 C 10 h in argon; prepared by the identical procedure without adding FeCl2.4H2O
Remarks: Initial discharge capacity 96.2 mAh/g at 0.5 C; only 84.3 mAh/g remains after 100 cycles. Single pair of voltage plateaus (Mn2+/Mn3+ only). Capacity loss ascribed to loss of electrochemical activity at the Mn2+/Mn3+ redox centre in olivine materials.

Paper_Title: Heat-rate-controlled hydrothermal crystallization of high-performance LiMn0.7Fe0.3PO4 cathode material for lithium-ion batteries

Synthesis_Method: Intermediate collected during the hydrothermal temperature-rising period at a heating rate of 3 C/min, filtered and dried
Remarks: Li3PO4 precipitates first on mixing; Fe2+ and Mn2+ then combine with free PO4^3- to give Fe3(PO4)2.8H2O (Ksp = 1.0e-36 at 25 C) and Mn3(PO4)2.7H2O (Ksp = 6.13e-32), both less soluble than Li3PO4 (Ksp = 3.2e-9), which drives Li3PO4 dissolution and reprecipitation of the metal phosphates.

Paper_Title: Heat-rate-controlled hydrothermal crystallization of high-performance LiMn0.7Fe0.3PO4 cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Composition_Formula: Hydrothermal intermediate at 80 C (Fe3(PO4)2.8H2O + Mn3(PO4)2.7H2O rich)
Synthesis_Method: Intermediate collected at 80 C during hydrothermal heating at 3 C/min
Remarks: Large amounts of Mn3(PO4)2.7H2O and Fe3(PO4)2.8H2O crystals have formed. The 2theta = 8.2 deg Mn3(PO4)2.7H2O peak shifts left versus P-60 C, implying expanded interplanar spacing (Bragg relation) and an unstable structure that leads to eventual dissolution of Mn3(PO4)2.7H2O.

Paper_Title: Heat-rate-controlled hydrothermal crystallization of high-performance LiMn0.7Fe0.3PO4 cathode material for lithium-ion batteries

Synthesis_Method: Intermediate collected at 120 C during hydrothermal heating at 3 C/min
Remarks: Mn3(PO4)2.7H2O peaks diminish markedly; free Mn2+ recombines with Fe2+ and PO4^3- to form M2(PO4)3.xH2O precipitates. Relatively weak LiMnPO4-type peaks appear at a temperature as low as 120 C - the hydrothermal formative temperature of LiMn0.7Fe0.3PO4, which is 10 C lower than that of LiFePO4 and can cause Li+/Fe2+ or Li+/Mn2+ dislocation.

Paper_Title: Heat-rate-controlled hydrothermal crystallization of high-performance LiMn0.7Fe0.3PO4 cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Hydrothermal reaction completed at 160 C (3 C/min heating rate)
Remarks: Above 140 C every reflection is attributed to LiMn0.7Fe0.3PO4. The synthesis is a three-step dissolution-precipitation process: precursor dissolution, nucleation and crystal growth. Slurry colour changes from light green (40 C) through deep green (130 C) to dark yellow (160 C).

Paper_Title: Highly efficient synthesis of nano LiMn0.90Fe0.10PO4/C composite via mechanochemical activation assisted calcination
Synthesis_Method: Mechanochemical activation assisted carbothermal reduction: stoichiometric Mn powder, Fe powder, LiH2PO4 and Li2CO3 (5% Li excess) mixed with polyvinyl alcohol as carbon source, dispersed in ethanol/deionized water/acetic acid (1:1:0.5 by volume) and ball-milled 4 h at 400 rpm with tungsten-carbide balls (ball:powder 20:1); precursor dried 60 C 15 h then calcined 700 C 6 h in Ar at a 3 C/min ramp; 0.3 g PVA added per 0.1 mol of LiMn0.9Fe0.1PO4 precursor
Remarks: Carbon content 0.38 wt% by infrared C-S analyser (HW 2000), from 0.3 g PVA per 0.1 mol precursor. Strongest XRD diffraction intensity of the series. XPS C 1s can be resolved into a C-C peak at 285 eV plus a transition-metal-carbide peak (Li-C or Mn-C) between 283 and 284 eV, because the carbon coating is very thin and XPS detects the interfacial carbide formed between reduced carbon and transition metal.

Paper_Title: Highly efficient synthesis of nano LiMn0.90Fe0.10PO4/C composite via mechanochemical activation assisted calcination

Paper_Title: Highly efficient synthesis of nano LiMn0.90Fe0.10PO4/C composite via mechanochemical activation assisted calcination

Paper_Title: Highly efficient synthesis of nano LiMn0.90Fe0.10PO4/C composite via mechanochemical activation assisted calcination

Paper_Title: Highly efficient synthesis of nano LiMn0.90Fe0.10PO4/C composite via mechanochemical activation assisted calcination
Synthesis_Method: Mechanochemical activation assisted carbothermal reduction: stoichiometric Mn powder, Fe powder, LiH2PO4 and Li2CO3 (5% Li excess) mixed with polyvinyl alcohol as carbon source, dispersed in ethanol/deionized water/acetic acid (1:1:0.5 by volume) and ball-milled 4 h at 400 rpm with tungsten-carbide balls (ball:powder 20:1); precursor dried 60 C 15 h then calcined 700 C 6 h in Ar at a 3 C/min ramp; 2.0 g PVA added per 0.1 mol of LiMn0.9Fe0.1PO4 precursor

Paper_Title: Effect of synthetic conditions on the electrochemical properties of LiMn0.4Fe0.6PO4/C synthesized by sol-gel technique

Paper_Title: Effect of synthetic conditions on the electrochemical properties of LiMn0.4Fe0.6PO4/C synthesized by sol-gel technique

Paper_Title: Effect of synthetic conditions on the electrochemical properties of LiMn0.4Fe0.6PO4/C synthesized by sol-gel technique

Remarks: Over 800 cycles at 0.5 C the voltage drop is only 0.167 V and the capacity drop only 17.7 mAh/g. Discharge average voltage falls from 3.95 V to 3.78 V, a minimal voltage decay of 0.21 mV per cycle - critical for practical large-scale application.

Paper_Title: Hierarchical LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 microspheres with atomic mixture of Fe/Mn derived from (Mn0.6Fe0.4)3(PO4)2.xH2O precursors for high stability lithium ion batteries

Remarks: Over 800 cycles at 0.5 C the voltage drop is 0.43 V and the capacity drop 95.4 mAh/g. Discharge average voltage falls from 3.85 V to 3.42 V.

Paper_Title: Hierarchical LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 microspheres with atomic mixture of Fe/Mn derived from (Mn0.6Fe0.4)3(PO4)2.xH2O precursors for high stability lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + wet sand milling + spray drying
Remarks: In situ XRD at 0.2 C over 2.5-4.5 V: continuous displacement of the (020), (311) and (121) reflections shows a unidirectional complete solid-solution evolution, attributed to the reduced primary particle size (<100 nm). During charge a and b axes and V decrease while c increases; changes are reversible on discharge. Volume change over (de)lithiation is 4.2%, and residual volume expansion after the first cycle is only 0.01 A^3.

Paper_Title: Hierarchical LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 microspheres with atomic mixture of Fe/Mn derived from (Mn0.6Fe0.4)3(PO4)2.xH2O precursors for high stability lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: High-speed wet sand milling + spray drying (separate Fe and Mn sources)
Remarks: In situ XRD at 0.2 C: solid-solution phase transition also occurs but less completely than in Precursor-LMFP. Volume change over (de)lithiation is 4.6% and the residual volume expansion after the first cycle is 0.07 A^3, substantially larger than the 0.01 A^3 of Precursor-LMFP.

Paper_Title: Hierarchical LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 microspheres with atomic mixture of Fe/Mn derived from (Mn0.6Fe0.4)3(PO4)2.xH2O precursors for high stability lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + wet sand milling + spray drying
Remarks: In situ XAFS: over 3.5-4 V the Fe K-edge XANES shifts strongly to higher energy (Fe2+ to Fe3+) and is invariant above 4.1 V; over 4-4.5 V the Mn K-edge shifts positively (Mn2+ to Mn3+). Edge shapes and positions of both Fe and Mn return to their original states after discharge, demonstrating highly reversible transition-metal redox. In the 4.0-4.5 V range the Mn-O coordination bifurcates into two elongated and four shortened bonds, the signature of Jahn-Teller distortion of MnO6, whereas FeO6 shows a unimodal Fe-O distribution throughout.

Paper_Title: Hierarchical LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 microspheres with atomic mixture of Fe/Mn derived from (Mn0.6Fe0.4)3(PO4)2.xH2O precursors for high stability lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + wet sand milling + spray drying
Remarks: After 800 cycles at 0.5 C the XRD peak positions and intensities are retained, and SEM shows the spherical secondary morphology of primary particles is preserved. ICP of cycled separators soaked in DMC shows significantly fewer dissolved Fe-Mn atoms than Blended-LMFP. After 100 cycles XAFS shows stabilised shorter M-O (M = Fe/Mn) bond lengths and a stabilised lower Fe oxidation state, i.e. higher Fe2+ retention that suppresses irreversible Fe3+ reduction.

Paper_Title: Hierarchical LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 microspheres with atomic mixture of Fe/Mn derived from (Mn0.6Fe0.4)3(PO4)2.xH2O precursors for high stability lithium ion batteries

Remarks: After 800 cycles at 0.5 C, significant peak shifts of the (101), (020) and (311) reflections and intensity reduction indicate structural distortion and crystallinity degradation; SEM shows surface smoothing and partial particle dissolution, correlating with transition-metal dissolution during cycling.

Paper_Title: Effect of firing temperature on the electrochemical performance of LiMn0.4Fe0.6PO4/C materials prepared by mechanical activation

Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Spray-dried route: 10 mmol Li2CO3, 12 mmol MnCO3, 8 mmol FePO4, 20 mmol NH4H2PO4 and 4 mmol glucose in deionized water ball-milled at a ball/powder ratio of 3, spray dried, calcined at 350 C for 4 h and sintered at 750 C for 8 h under Ar/H2. SEM shows micron-sized spherical secondary particles assembled from 200-300 nm primary nanoparticles with a homogeneous narrow size distribution and a loose, porous surface favourable for electrolyte wetting. Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel

SEM shows an irregular morphology of aggregated nanoparticles with smaller and more widely distributed particle size, reducing tap density. BET specific surface area 14.21 m2/g. Relative XRD diffraction intensity weaker than LMFP-D, consistent with smaller grain size.

Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Raman D band at ~1355 cm-1 and G band at ~1595 cm-1; intensity ratio ID/IG = 0.845, lower than LMFP-S, reflecting enhanced graphitization of the carbon coating. Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel

Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Rietveld refinement with the FullProf Suite and a pseudo-Voigt profile: R-factors Rwp and Rp of approximately 1-3% and chi-squared below 3. LMFP-D has smaller lattice constants a and c and a smaller cell volume than LMFP-S, indicating a more compact crystal structure; the shortened c-axis suggests a less distorted and more stable Li+ transport pathway, lowering the activation energy for ion hopping and reducing lattice strain during cycling. Numerical lattice parameters for both LMFP-D and LMFP-S are given only in supplementary Tables S2-S3.

Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: EDS mapping shows uniform dispersion of Fe, Mn, P and O. Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel

Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density

Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density

Paper_Title: Morphology effects on LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 cathode for lithium-ion batteries with high energy density

Remarks: Chemical delithiation of LiMnPO4 is far slower than for y < 0.8 and induces significant peak broadening. Paper_Title: Crystal Chemistry of the Olivine-Type Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 and (MnyFe1-y)PO4 as Possible 4 V Cathode Materials for Lithium Batteries
Source_PDF: Journal of Chemistry - 2019 - Huynh - Structure and Electrochemical Behavior of Minor Mn‐Doped Olivine LiMnxFe1 xPO4.pdf
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy ball milling + sintering)
Remarks: Across the lithiated Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 series the orthorhombic lattice expands isotropically with Mn2+ content and the unit cell volume increases monotonically, giving a stable complete solid solution. Explained by Pauling ionic radii: high-spin Mn2+ (3d5) is 0.97 A versus high-spin Fe2+ (3d6) at 0.92 A. Expansion reaches roughly 1-1.5% in a, b and c at y = 1 relative to y = 0.

Paper_Title: Crystal Chemistry of the Olivine-Type Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 and (MnyFe1-y)PO4 as Possible 4 V Cathode Materials for Lithium Batteries
Source_PDF: Journal of Chemistry - 2019 - Huynh - Structure and Electrochemical Behavior of Minor Mn‐Doped Olivine LiMnxFe1 xPO4.pdf
Synthesis_Method: Chemical delithiation with NO2BF4 in acetonitrile
Remarks: Across the delithiated (MnyFe1-y)PO4 series the unit cell volume stays almost constant independent of Mn3+ content, because high-spin Mn3+ (3d4, 0.79 A) and high-spin Fe3+ (3d5, 0.79 A) have almost the same ionic radius. Elongation of the a axis (to about +1.5% at y = 0.8) is compensated by shrinkage of the b axis (to about -1.5%) and slight shrinkage of c, and the anisotropic distortion increases linearly with Mn3+ content, indicating the strong electron (3d4) lattice Jahn-Teller interaction.

Paper_Title: Crystal Chemistry of the Olivine-Type Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 and (MnyFe1-y)PO4 as Possible 4 V Cathode Materials for Lithium Batteries
Source_PDF: Journal of Chemistry - 2019 - Huynh - Structure and Electrochemical Behavior of Minor Mn‐Doped Olivine LiMnxFe1 xPO4.pdf
Synthesis_Method: Chemical delithiation with NO2BF4 in acetonitrile
Remarks: Under the constant-volume condition, strain energy accumulates in the lattice as the Mn3+ content increases, so the Fe3+PO4-Mn3+PO4 binary system is flawed at large manganese content (y > 0.8). Because the Mn3+/Mn2+ redox proceeds in a two-phase manner by a first-order transition between the Jahn-Teller active Mn3+ phase with cooperative elastic deformation and the Jahn-Teller inactive Mn2+ phase, stable cathode performance is achieved only for y < 0.8; this accounts for the abrupt capacity decrease above that composition.

Paper_Title: Crystal Chemistry of the Olivine-Type Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 and (MnyFe1-y)PO4 as Possible 4 V Cathode Materials for Lithium Batteries
Source_PDF: Journal of Chemistry - 2019 - Huynh - Structure and Electrochemical Behavior of Minor Mn‐Doped Olivine LiMnxFe1 xPO4.pdf
Remarks: Spin-polarized FP-LAPW (Wien97) DFT with gradient-corrected exchange-correlation, lmax = 10, plane-wave cutoff 36.0 Ry (RMT K = 7.2), 126 k points. Total DOS of LiFePO4: narrow band near the Fermi level assigned to Fe 3d with antibonding eg and nonbonding t2g states identifiable despite Cs-induced degeneracy; dispersed O s and p states from -10 to -3 eV. Spin-up 3d states completely filled with a spin-down peak 0.8 eV below the Fermi level. Integrated magnetic moment 3.8 uB per LiFePO4 unit, close to the 4 uB expected for high-spin 3d6 Fe2+.

Paper_Title: Crystal Chemistry of the Olivine-Type Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 and (MnyFe1-y)PO4 as Possible 4 V Cathode Materials for Lithium Batteries

Remarks: Total DOS of FePO4: with removal of lithium the spin-down d band becomes totally unoccupied and a bandgap of 0.5 eV appears. Calculated magnetic moment 4.8 uB per FePO4 unit, very close to the 5 uB of high-spin 3d5 Fe3+ in the crystal-field model.

Remarks: Highly distorted FeO6 octahedra with Cs symmetry in LiFePO4 (atomic positions from ref. 18): Fe-O1 = 2.21 A, Fe-O2 = 2.11 A, Fe-O3 = 2.06 A (two bonds) and Fe-O3 = 2.25 A (two bonds), with O-Fe-O angles of 91.0, 119.5, 65.8 and 89.0 degrees. Paper_Title: Crystal Chemistry of the Olivine-Type Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 and (MnyFe1-y)PO4 as Possible 4 V Cathode Materials for Lithium Batteries

Paper_Title: Crystal Chemistry of the Olivine-Type Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 and (MnyFe1-y)PO4 as Possible 4 V Cathode Materials for Lithium Batteries
Source_PDF: Journal of Chemistry - 2019 - Huynh - Structure and Electrochemical Behavior of Minor Mn‐Doped Olivine LiMnxFe1 xPO4.pdf
Remarks: Cited systematic study by Padhi et al. on Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 with y = 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.0, reporting that the width of the 4.1 V Mn3+/Mn2+ plateau relative to the 3.4 V Fe3+/Fe2+ plateau increases with Mn content y but that the total capacity drops rapidly above y = 0.75. Padhi et al. stressed the importance of Fe in near neighbours through Fe3+-O-Mn2+ superexchange interactions destabilising the Mn2+ level, and showed the 4.1 V capacity cannot be achieved unless Fe and Mn coexist at the octahedral 4c site.

Remarks: Cell details: cathode a highly homogeneous mixture of Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 : carbon black : PVDF in a weight ratio of 90:8:2, coin-type cells (size 2025) with lithium metal anodes and 1 M LiPF6 in propylene carbonate/dimethyl carbonate. Paper_Title: Crystal Chemistry of the Olivine-Type Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 and (MnyFe1-y)PO4 as Possible 4 V Cathode Materials for Lithium Batteries
Source_PDF: Journal of Chemistry - 2019 - Huynh - Structure and Electrochemical Behavior of Minor Mn‐Doped Olivine LiMnxFe1 xPO4.pdf
Synthesis_Method: Chemical delithiation with NO2BF4 in acetonitrile
Remarks: Chemical oxidation protocol: 8.5 g NO2BF4 dissolved in 300 mL acetonitrile, then 5 g of Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 added and stirred 24 h at room temperature with purified Ar bubbling, per Li(MnyFe1-y)PO4 + NO2BF4 to (MnyFe1-y)PO4 + LiBF4 + NO2. NO2BF4 was added at twice the stoichiometric amount to encourage complete reaction. Products filtered, washed and vacuum dried, then analysed by ICP-AES for exact composition. Lattice constants calculated by least squares with a Si standard from slow-scan (0.5 deg/min) XRD.

Paper_Title: Three-dimensional (3D) LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanoflowers assembled from interconnected nanoflakes as cathode materials for lithium ion batteries

Because the nanoflowers are interconnected and porous, the carbon coating extends into the inner surfaces. Lattice fringes of width 0.356 nm correspond to the d-spacing of the (111) planes of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4.

Paper_Title: Three-dimensional (3D) LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanoflowers assembled from interconnected nanoflakes as cathode materials for lithium ion batteries

Paper_Title: Three-dimensional (3D) LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanoflowers assembled from interconnected nanoflakes as cathode materials for lithium ion batteries

Remarks: Mode near 944 cm-1 relates to the PO4(3-) stretching vibration. Broad D band (disordered sp3 carbon) at about 1339 cm-1 and G band (graphitic sp2) at about 1578 cm-1. Paper_Title: Three-dimensional (3D) LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanoflowers assembled from interconnected nanoflakes as cathode materials for lithium ion batteries

Paper_Title: Three-dimensional (3D) LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanoflowers assembled from interconnected nanoflakes as cathode materials for lithium ion batteries

Paper_Title: Three-dimensional (3D) LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanoflowers assembled from interconnected nanoflakes as cathode materials for lithium ion batteries

Paper_Title: Three-dimensional (3D) LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanoflowers assembled from interconnected nanoflakes as cathode materials for lithium ion batteries

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: 0.2 mol H3PO4 (85 wt%) added to 100 mL deionised water, then 0.0133 mol Fe3O4 dispersed in; H2O2 (30 wt%) added dropwise as oxidant and the mixture heated to 90 C with stirring for 2 h to a white liquid. 0.16 mol MnO2 added and ground 10 min at 400 rpm, then H2O2 added as reductant and MnO2 fully reduced by 2 h ball milling. After dilution with 200 mL water, 0.8 g PVP, 3 g beta-cyclodextrin and stoichiometric Li2CO3 were added as dispersant, carbon and lithium sources; 2 h ball milling then 1 h horizontal sand milling at 1000 rpm, spray drying, and sintering at 650 C for 6 h under flowing argon at 3 C/min.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Diffraction peaks index to the orthorhombic olivine structure (JCPDS 74-0375/83-2092); strong sharp peaks indicate highly crystalline LMFP and no carbon crystal or impurity peak is detected, so the coated carbon is amorphous. Local amplification shows the peak positions are slightly offset from LiMnPO4 (74-0375) and LiFePO4 (83-2092), proving successful Fe doping at the Mn site. Cell refinement (MDI Jade 6): a = 6.082 A, b = 10.421 A, c = 4.731 A, V = 299.84 A3, smaller than LiMnPO4 (6.106/10.454/4.749, 303.14 A3) because Fe2+ has a smaller ionic radius (0.92 nm quoted) than Mn2+ (0.97 nm quoted); LiFePO4 reference is 6.010/10.334/4.693, 291.50 A3.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Fine quasi-spherical secondary particles of 3-10 um with many irregular concave and convex surface structures formed during spray drying; at the nanometre scale the primary particle size is about 50 nm and the nanoscale primary particles are tightly bound. During spray drying the precursor slurry is atomised into droplets that dry and condense into spherical secondary particles under hot blast air. EDS mapping (Fig. S1) shows Mn, Fe, O, P and C evenly distributed.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: LMFP nanocrystals are tightly bound into a continuous conformal conducting carbon network, and the contours of individual LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanocrystalline grains cannot be distinctly resolved because of the dense microsphere structure. A clear lattice fringe of 2.31 A is assigned to the (012) plane, and a continuous conformal carbon layer of about 3 nm coats the nanocrystal surface. Carbon content of the prepared LMFP is 2.3 wt%. Since Li+ diffuses one-dimensionally along the b axis, the diffusion path in the 50 nm nanocrystal is only about 50 nm.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Reversible discharge capacity 159.1 mAh/g at 0.1C over 2.5-4.5 V, approaching the theoretical 170 mAh/g. Two clear stable voltage platforms near 3.5 V and 4.1 V correspond to the Fe3+/Fe2+ and Mn3+/Mn2+ redox couples.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Discharge capacity 153.1 mAh/g at 0.5C, 96.2% of the 0.1C capacity.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Discharge capacity 146.8 mAh/g at 1C, 92.3% of the 0.1C capacity.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Discharge capacity 142.9 mAh/g at 2C, 89.8% of the 0.1C capacity.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Discharge capacity 136.3 mAh/g at 5C, 85.7% of the 0.1C capacity.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Specific discharge capacity 129.1 mAh/g even at 10C, 81.1% of the 0.1C capacity, showing outstanding high-rate performance. Ascribed to the LMFP nanocrystalline primary particles and the conformal carbon coating, which shortens the Li diffusion distance and improves electronic conductivity.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Cells charged at 0.5C and discharged at 1C: after 1000 cycles the specific discharge capacity is maintained at 140.2 mAh/g with 95% capacity retention and a loss of only 0.0073 mAh/g per cycle, superior to similar materials in the literature. Median discharge voltage is 3.92 V in the initial cycle with only 0.16 V attenuation after 1000 cycles. Attributed to Fe doping reducing Mn3+ content and alleviating Mn dissolution, and to the conformal carbon protecting against HF attack.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: At 0.1 mV/s four peaks appear at 3.481 V / 3.597 V and 3.905 V / 4.196 V, corresponding to the Fe2+/Fe3+ and Mn2+/Mn3+ redox reactions and to the two charge/discharge platforms. Small potential differences and excellent peak symmetry reflect high reversibility and small polarisation.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Peak current Ip is proportional to nu^1/2, indicating a diffusion-controlled Li+ process. Li+ diffusion rates from the fit: anodic Fe 1.54e-11, anodic Mn 2.94e-11, cathodic Fe 1.02e-11 and cathodic Mn 4.96e-11 cm2/s, i.e. 1.0-4.9e-11 cm2/s overall. Parameters used: F = 96500 C/mol, T = 298 K, CLi = 2.23e-5 mol/L, R = 8.314 J/mol/K, n = 0.2 for Fe2+/Fe3+ and n = 0.8 for Mn2+/Mn3+. The cathodic Mn value is entered in the diffusion column; see this remark for the full set.
Evidence: Fig. 3e; Table 2 (Li+ diffusion from Randles-Sevcik fit)

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Before cycling the single LMFP electrode shows the largest charge-transfer resistance of the set at 39.8 Ohm (NCA is smallest at 15.3 Ohm), reflecting the faster early-stage kinetics of NCA. After 200 cycles at 1C in the charged state at 4.5 V, LMFP still exhibits a small Rct of 89.1 Ohm, reflecting good cycling stability. EIS from 100 kHz to 0.005 Hz with 5 mV AC oscillation.
Evidence: Fig. 8b-c, Table S3 (EIS fresh and after 200 cycles)

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Commercial material (CNGR Advanced Material Co., Ltd.)
Remarks: Single NCA shows the smallest fresh Rct of 15.3 Ohm but after 200 cycles the plot develops two semicircles with a surface film resistance Rf of 8.4 Ohm and Rct rising dramatically from 15.3 to 221.7 Ohm, closely related to severe side reactions between NCA and the electrolyte which increase the interface resistance to e-/Li+ transport.
Evidence: Fig. 8b-c, Table S3 (EIS fresh and after 200 cycles)

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Commercial material (CNGR Advanced Material Co., Ltd.)
Remarks: Pristine NCA shows secondary spherical particles in the 5-10 um size range with a primary particle size of 200-500 nm.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: After rolling at 0.03 mm the LMFP electrode has a flatter surface than the NCA electrode, confirming good flexibility of the LMFP particles. Reducing the rolling height to 0.02 mm makes the LMFP surface smoother and denser with no cracks on the LMFP microspheres, whereas cracks appear in the NCA microspheres under the same condition. EDS of the 75%NCA electrode shows NCA particles embedded in LMFP particles like gems, reducing electrolyte/NCA contact.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Physical blending (grinding) of flexible LMFP microspheres with commercial NCA
Remarks: DSC of electrode material with electrolyte at 1:1 mass ratio: onset temperature raised to 231 C (200 C for pristine NCA), maximal heat flow only 0.99 W/g versus 2.18 W/g for NCA, and total released heat 700.7 J/g versus a calculated (rule-of-mixtures) value of 935.0 J/g, a reduction of 234.3 J/g. Indicates a thermal protection effect of LMFP on NCA and greatly reduced risk of severe thermal runaway.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Commercial material (CNGR Advanced Material Co., Ltd.)
Remarks: Four exothermic peaks with an onset temperature of 200 C: two connected peaks between 200 and 260 C from electrolyte decomposition and electrolyte/electrode oxidation, a sharp peak at 270 C from combustion of O2 released by NCA with the electrolyte, and a fourth near 315 C from decomposition of remaining electrolyte and NCA. Maximal heat flow 2.18 W/g and total released heat 1219.0 J/g.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: LMFP shows an onset temperature of 268 C, a maximal heat flow of only 0.45 W/g and a total released heat of just 83.0 J/g. The second exothermic peak is attributed to partial loss of oxygen from the Mn0.8Fe0.2PO4 phase with generation of (Mn0.8Fe0.2)2P2O7. Unsaturated PO4(3-) groups on the LMFP surface are believed to capture PF5, which catalyses electrolyte decomposition, thus inhibiting it.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Commercial material (CNGR Advanced Material Co., Ltd.)
Remarks: Discharge specific capacities of single NCA are 205.6, 198.6, 191.7, 183.7, 172.7 and 158.6 mAh/g at 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 10C respectively over 2.5-4.5 V; NCA shows the highest discharge capacity at all rates among the electrodes compared.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Physical blending (grinding) of flexible LMFP microspheres with commercial NCA
Remarks: Discharge capacity 196.4 mAh/g at 0.1C. Capacity retention 90.1% after 200 cycles at 1C over 2.5-4.3 V (NCA 82.6%), and 88.9% over 2.5-4.5 V where pristine NCA falls to 73.3%. Two extra voltage platforms near 3.5 V and 4.1 V from the Fe2+/Fe3+ and Mn2+/Mn3+ couples appear in the blend curves and become clearer as LMFP content rises.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Physical blending (grinding) of flexible LMFP microspheres with commercial NCA
Remarks: Discharge capacity 184.3 mAh/g at 0.1C; capacity retention 91.9% after 200 cycles at 1C over 2.5-4.3 V.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Physical blending (grinding) of flexible LMFP microspheres with commercial NCA
Remarks: Discharge capacity 170.8 mAh/g at 0.1C; capacity retention 95.2% after 200 cycles at 1C over 2.5-4.3 V, the best of the blends, showing cycle performance improves monotonically with LMFP content.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Commercial material (CNGR Advanced Material Co., Ltd.)
Remarks: Pristine NCA gives the worst cycle performance: 82.6% retention after 200 cycles at 1C over 2.5-4.3 V, falling to 73.3% when the cut-off is raised to 4.5 V.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Physical blending (grinding) of flexible LMFP microspheres with commercial NCA
Remarks: In-situ XRD of the 75%NCA electrode over 2.5-4.5 V: at the initial stage the (211) and (311) peaks of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 shift continuously, an explicit sign of solid-solution phase transformation connected with Fe2+/Fe3+ redox (stage 1). An irreversible structural transition follows as the NCA (104) peak shifts to higher angle. A new Mn0.8Fe0.2PO4 phase then appears from Mn2+/Mn3+ redox in Li0.8Mn0.8Fe0.2PO4 (stage 2). A small overpotential peak in the initial charge-discharge curve disappears in later cycles, generally ascribed to activation of NCA particles in the blend cathode.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Physical blending (grinding) of flexible LMFP microspheres with commercial NCA
Remarks: For single NCA, three pairs of redox peaks correspond to the H1-M, M-H2 and H2-H3 phase transitions, and the H1-to-M salient peak voltage drops from 3.885 V (first cycle) to 3.768 V (second cycle) on activation. In blends the prominent anodic peak shifts right through overlap of the NCA peaks with the LMFP Mn2+/Mn3+ peak, indicating NCA and LMFP participate simultaneously in the redox process. After 200 cycles many impurities are deposited on the Li anode of the NCA cell but far fewer for 75%NCA and LMFP; ICP confirms deposited Ni, Co and Al on the anode decrease significantly after blending LMFP.
Evidence: Fig. 8a (CV, 0.1 mV/s); Fig. S9, Table S2 (anode ICP)

Paper_Title: Synthesis of flexible LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C microsphere and its synergetic effects with blended LiNi0.85Co0.10Al0.05O2 electrodes
Synthesis_Method: Scalable solid-state route: wet chemical + ball/sand milling + spray drying + sintering
Remarks: Flexible LMFP microspheres prepared from cheap Fe3O4 and electrolytic MnO2 by a scalable solid-state method deliver 159.1, 153.1, 146.8, 142.9, 136.3 and 129.1 mAh/g at 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 10C, with a Li+ diffusion rate of 1.02-4.96e-11 cm2/s. Under roller pressure NCA particles become embedded in the flexible LMFP microspheres, so the blend combines the thermal stability of LMFP with the energy density of NCA.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: MWNTs (Hanwha Nanotech) grown by CVD with average diameter 10 nm, length 10 um and purity 95%, functionalized with carboxyl groups in concentrated H2SO4:HNO3 3:1 at 3 M acid concentration, soaked at 80 C for 10 h, washed to pH 7 and vacuum heated at 120 C overnight. m-LMFP made by milling the LMFP precursors together with KBs and MWNTs (7 g raw material, hardened-Cr-SUS balls of 12.70 mm x2 and 6.35 mm x4, Spex Certiprep 5000M, 1 h, Ar-purged 3 h), pressing to a pellet at 1000 psi for 5 min and sintering at 600 C for 12 h under purified N2. KB+MWNT loading fixed at 6 wt% with KB:MWNT varied 0:6, 1:5, 3:3, 5:1 and 6:0.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: All diffraction peaks index to an orthorhombic structure with Pnmb space group. Lattice parameters of the m-LMFP with 1 wt% MWNT + 5 wt% KB by least squares: a = 4.73412 A, b = 10.42641 A, c = 6.08362 A, in good agreement with JCPDS 33-0804. No secondary phases such as Li3PO4, Mn2P2O7 or Fe3P because mixing and calcination were done under Ar purge. The (111), (211) and (311) peak intensity ratio differs slightly from the card, attributed to cation mixing during calcination or unit cell volume changes from the Fe2+/Mn2+ ionic radius difference. Adding MWNTs causes no shift in the XRD pattern.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Composition_Formula: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 (m-LMFP with pristine vs functionalized MWNT)
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Spectra consist mainly of D and G bands at 1350 and 1580 cm-1. LMFP with pristine MWNT/KB shows a sharp band at 945 cm-1 from the symmetric Ag (v1) PO4 mode and weaker bands at 997 and 1058 cm-1 from the asymmetric v3 modes of (PO4)3-. The 945 cm-1 band is relatively weak for LMFP with functionalized MWNT/KB owing to the screening effect of carbon, and the close similarity of the spectra indicates that f-MWNTs are uniformly dispersed on the KB-LMFP surface.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Average particle size about 100 nm with the KB/MWNT mixture uniformly dispersed between the LMFP particles. Chemical modification of the MWNT sidewalls gives good dispersion and effective networking. Aggregates of unmodified MWNTs blocked dispersion into the cathode particles and could not bridge the particles effectively, giving wide contact points and high internal resistance. MWNTs mixed with precursors before calcination were partially fractured but still networked; MWNTs blended only with finished LMFP particles kept their original length.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: MWNTs are clearly uncapped when mixed with the LMFP precursors, whereas some capped MWNTs remain when mixed after lithiation. Uncapping is induced by embrittlement of the nanotubes during lithiation, with hoop stress along the circumferential direction of a lithiated MWNT assisting breakage. TEM-EDS confirmed a thin amorphous layer of about 2 nm composed of LiMnxFe1-xPO4 formed around the MWNTs, which is thought to facilitate more efficient Li-ion diffusion between m-LMFP particles.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: First discharge capacity 158.4 mAh/g for the 6 wt% KB-only sample (CC-CV at C/20 to 4.5 V, held until C/100, discharged to 2.0 V; 1C = 170 mAh/g). Carbon black near the cathode particles tends to block crystal growth during calcination, so KB-rich samples have the smallest crystal size.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Highest first discharge capacity of the series, 162.7 mAh/g, close to the theoretical value, for the optimal KB:MWNT ratio of 5:1 at a total additive content of 6 wt%. Above 1 wt% MWNT the specific capacity decreases gradually with increasing MWNT content.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: First discharge capacity 156.5 mAh/g for the 3:3 KB:MWNT ratio.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: First discharge capacity 152.7 mAh/g for the 1:5 KB:MWNT ratio.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Lowest first discharge capacity of the series, 150.0 mAh/g, for MWNT only. Complete replacement of KB by MWNT does not increase specific capacity despite improved electrical properties, because it is difficult to surround the particles with only CNTs given their high aspect ratio, so crystal growth is not suppressed.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Modified LMFP with etched and functionalized MWNTs gives discharge capacities of 162 mAh/g at 0.1C and 147 mAh/g at 1C, described as the highest values reported to date for this type of electrode. Cathode materials containing well-dispersed etched MWNTs outperform those with pristine or merely etched MWNTs.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: The electrode with 1 wt% MWNT shows better rate performance than both the pristine sample and the 6 wt% MWNT sample, retaining 99%, 95% and 90% of its 0.1C capacity at discharge rates of 0.2, 0.5 and 1C. Charge rate fixed at 0.1C while the discharge rate was raised from 0.05C to 1C.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: The pristine (KB-only) sample and the 6 wt% MWNT sample both retained only 85% of their discharge capacity at 1C, versus 90% for the optimal 5:1 KB:MWNT electrode.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Specific resistance of m-LMFP falls exponentially with increasing MWNT content in the hybrid additive; above 3 wt% MWNT the resistivity decreases only gradually, indicating that the conductivity enhancement from substituting KB with MWNT saturates and that the nanoparticles and hybrid additives are already sufficiently wired at low MWNT fraction. Less MWNT is required than KB because MWNTs offer more electronic transport channels.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: High-frequency semicircle radius of approximately 22.47 Ohm after the first cycle at room temperature. Impedance measured from 100 mHz to 100 kHz with 10 mVrms amplitude.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Lowest cell resistance of the five cells, with a semicircle radius of approximately 18.09 Ohm, in agreement with its highest specific capacity.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Semicircle radius of approximately 33.57 Ohm; AC impedance increases gradually with MWNT content above 1 wt%, in contrast to the trend of the four-point-probe specific resistance.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Semicircle radius of approximately 41.95 Ohm. Excess fractured CNTs act as a source of resistance through many point contacts and impede charge transfer.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Largest semicircle radius of approximately 46.61 Ohm. Electrochemical performance of the m-LMFP cell is therefore related to charge-transfer resistance rather than to bulk electrical resistance of the material.

Paper_Title: High-performance LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with hybrid conductive additives based on functionalized and etched multi-walled carbon nanotubes by self-destruction during the lithiation process
Synthesis_Method: Solid-state reaction (high-energy milling, pelletising and calcination)
Remarks: Warburg impedance, inversely proportional to ionic conductivity, increased as more MWNTs replaced KB particles, so ionic conductivity in the electrode decreased above 1 wt% MWNT. Combined with the XRD crystal size data this implies that ionic conductivity and cell performance depend mainly on crystal size rather than electrical conductivity. Paper_Title: Superior electronic/ionic kinetics of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C nanoparticles cathode by doping strategy toward enhanced Li-ion storage

Remarks: Operando XRD over 2.5-4.5 V at 0.5C shows a typical LixMn0.8Fe0.15Ni0.05PO4 (0<x<1) phase transition. Those peaks then shift continuously to higher angles, indicating a solid solution reaction in the high-voltage region above 4.2 V and an amorphous solid solution zone between the two phases. On discharge the delithiated phase peaks disappear while the lithiated peaks recover, demonstrating fully reversible lithiation and a combined two-phase plus solid solution mechanism.

Paper_Title: Superior electronic/ionic kinetics of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C nanoparticles cathode by doping strategy toward enhanced Li-ion storage

Qualitatively, Ni2+ reduces the degree of ordering of the atomic arrangements in the solid solution and weakens the ionic bonding energy between the backbone ions and Li+, while also catalysing formation of sp2 graphitised carbon during pyrolysis of the organic carbon source.

CTAB (0.002 mol) dissolved in 30 mL ultrapure water at 50 C was injected slowly into the suspension under vigorous stirring, and the slurry was stirred at 85 C then dried at 120 C for 12 h in a vacuum oven. Oxalic acid plays a dual role: its ionised carboxyl groups form a highly stable coordination compound with Mn to maintain the divalent state, and the solution has a robust reducing ability preventing Mn2+ oxidation, so no pH control is needed.

Electrodes were 80 : 10 : 10 active material : acetylene black : PVDF in NMP on Al foil, dried at 120 C for 12 h, punched to 14 mm discs with a mass loading around 2.0 mg.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries

Remarks: Main peaks of the precursors index to MnHPO4.2.25H2O (JCPDS 49-0199). MP-0 (no oxalic acid) shows weak diffraction and strong diffuse intensity, confirming poor crystallinity. Elemental mapping shows Mn, P and O uniformly distributed. The topology of the metal phosphate layer in the ac face of MnHPO4 resembles that in the bc face of LiMnPO4, so the transformation proceeds without major structural rearrangement, with H atoms in the MnHPO4 channels replaced by Li+.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries

Remarks: Diffraction peaks are sharper and stronger than the unsintered precursors and match single-phase olivine orthorhombic LiMnPO4 (JCPDS 74-0375). No impurity peaks and no carbon diffraction peaks are observed, so the pyrolytic carbon from phenolic resin and unreacted oxalic acid is amorphous.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries

Remarks: Intense bands around 900-1100 cm-1 are assigned to the intramolecular stretching modes of the PO4(3-) group and are similar across samples, indicating the same olivine LiMnPO4 crystal structure. Two strong broad peaks at 1334 and 1584 cm-1 are the D and G bands. The fitted ID/IG is 0.933 for LMFP-0.5 versus 0.937 for LMFP-0, a slight decrease after adding oxalic acid, so LMFP-0.5 has a marginally higher graphitisation degree; the highly graphitic coating acts as a conductive network preventing crystal growth and providing a fast electron transfer channel.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate + high-energy ball milling and calcination
Remarks: XPS spectra of LMFP-0.5 and LMFP-0 contain Li, Mn, Fe, P, O and C. Li 1s, P 2p and O 1s appear at 56.4, 133.4 and 532.8 eV, and the strong C 1s peak at 284.65 eV shows pyrolytic carbon well coated on the crystal surface. Fe 2p peaks at 710.75, 714.32, 724.20 and 727.98 eV with a coupling peak and two satellite peaks are consistent with Fe2+, and the 13.45 eV separation between Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 demonstrates Fe2+ in the olivine and replacement of some Mn by Fe. Mn 2p peaks at 641.32, 642.78, 645.33 (shake-up satellite) and 654.04 eV reveal Mn2+. ICP-OES gives a practical molar ratio Li : Mn : Fe : P of 1.040 : 0.806 : 0.191 : 1.000, close to the 1.05 : 0.8 : 0.2 : 1 stoichiometry.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate + high-energy ball milling and calcination
Remarks: Without oxalic acid the nanoparticles are irregular in shape with rough surfaces and wide granularity. All materials contain micrometre-sized secondary particles agglomerated from nanometre-sized primary particles, and the morphology is far more homogeneous after high-energy ball milling than in the precursor.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate + high-energy ball milling and calcination
Remarks: Particle morphology is regular with uniform distribution, similar to ellipsoidal nanoparticles of grain size 50-100 nm, some contacting to form large micron-sized particles. No single conductive carbon film was observed, indicating the nanoparticle surfaces are connected by a carbon coating layer generating a soft agglomeration structure and improving bulk density. An amorphous carbon layer about 3 nm thick covers the surface, confirmed by the concentric-circle FFT pattern. Interplanar spacings of 4.32 A and 3.57 A correspond to the (101) and (111) lattice planes, and the FFT indexes to the [010] zone axis with the dominant (010) plane growing along the [010] axis, favouring a high Li+ diffusion coefficient. EDS gives P : (Mn + Fe) = 1 : 0.977 against the theoretical 1 : 1, with 23.67% pyrolytic carbon on the surface.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate + high-energy ball milling and calcination
Remarks: At the highest oxalic acid level the pyrolytic carbon layer between particles thickens, aggravating agglomeration and increasing particle size. Particle size is still about 300 nm but irregular granular agglomeration occurs with nanoparticles wrapped in a large amount of pyrolytic carbon (64.35% by EDS). Grains are surrounded by an ultra-thick carbon layer of more than about 20 nm, formed by high-temperature sintering of unreacted excess oxalic acid. Distinct lattice fringes of 3.02 A correspond to the (020) plane. The serious grain agglomeration hinders Li ion migration and the thick carbon lengthens the transmission distance, lowering tap density.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate + high-energy ball milling and calcination
Remarks: Typical type-IV isotherm with an evident hysteresis loop at high relative pressure (P/P0 = 0.45-1), indicating a mesoporous structure, with pore diameters mainly distributed around 20-50 nm. Specific surface area 59.01 m2/g, higher than LMFP-0, attributed to pyrolysis of the redundant oxalic acid producing an ordered mesoporous structure that gives closer contact between nanoparticles and more active sites for Li+ insertion/extraction.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries

Remarks: Specific surface area 55.14 m2/g with pore diameters mainly distributed around 20-50 nm and a type-IV isotherm, slightly lower than LMFP-0.5.

Paper_Title: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4@C cathode prepared via a novel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate for high performance lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel hydrated MnHPO4 intermediate + high-energy ball milling and calcination
Remarks: CV recorded at 0.1 mV/s over 2.5-4.8 V. The two peak pairs a/a' and b/b' correspond to the Mn2+/Mn3+ and Fe2+/Fe3+ redox couples. Remarks: In the initial 100 cycles at 0.05C the discharge capacity drops from 153.9 to 147.5 mAh/g, a retention of 95.84%. Paper_Title: High Surface Area Carbon Composite LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 as High-Power Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries
Synthesis_Method: High-energy ball milling solid-state synthesis + wet mixing of high surface area carbon
Remarks: Stoichiometric LiH2PO4, MnCO3 and FeC2O4.2H2O were mixed in a high-energy ball mill (Retsch PM 100) at 400 rpm for 8 h with an agate ball-to-material ratio of 20 : 1, then heat treated at 550 C for 12 h under Ar-H2. Composites were made by dispersing 4, 6 or 8 wt% high surface area carbon (China Steel Corporation, 2500 m2/g) in ethanol, drying in a vacuum oven at 90 C for 10-12 h, and a further heat treatment at 550 C for 6 h in inert atmosphere. Electrodes were 80% active material, 10% PVDF and 10% Super C-65 in NMP, doctor-blade coated on 20 um Al foil, dried overnight at 90 C, calendered and punched to 10 mm discs with a loading of about 4 mg/cm2.

Paper_Title: High Surface Area Carbon Composite LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 as High-Power Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries

Paper_Title: High Surface Area Carbon Composite LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 as High-Power Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries

Paper_Title: High Surface Area Carbon Composite LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 as High-Power Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries

Remarks: Particles are almost spherical and nanometric, approximately 50-80 nm from the zoomed image. HSAC itself has a small granular morphology, and all three composites show a similar morphology to pristine LMFP, so HSAC does not change the structure on the nanometre scale but boosts electrochemical performance.

Paper_Title: High Surface Area Carbon Composite LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 as High-Power Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries

Paper_Title: High Surface Area Carbon Composite LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 as High-Power Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries

Paper_Title: High Surface Area Carbon Composite LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 as High-Power Electrodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries

Paper_Title: Double-Structured LiMn0.85Fe0.15PO4 Coordinated with LiFePO4 for Rechargeable Lithium Batteries

Remarks: Rietveld refinement of the thermally lithiated product with a 0.5 um outer layer. FIB cross-section, TEM and EELS show numerous pores in both bulk and outer layer, denser agglomeration of the smaller LiFePO4 primary particles in the outer layer, and a carbon layer covering the primary particles and the outer surface at the tens-of-nm level. EPMA indicates a sharp interface with no LiFePO4 in the bulk and no LiMnPO4 in the outer layer.
