Paper_Title: Co-precipitation synthesis of micro-sized spherical LiMn0.5Fe0.5PO4 cathode material for lithium batteries
Source_PDF: Advanced Materials - 2011 - Sun - Micrometer‐Sized  Nanoporous  High‐Volumetric‐Capacity LiMn0 85Fe0 15PO4 Cathode Material.pdf
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation of (Mn1-xFex)3(PO4)2.xH2O hydrate, dehydration, then thermal lithiation with Li3PO4 and pitch carbon coating
Remarks: Summary rate figures: 142 mAh/(g-phosphate) at C/20 and 101 mAh/(g-phosphate) at 1C, comparable to the nano-sized version despite 15 um secondary particles. The authors attribute this to two features working together - nanopores that let electrolyte penetrate and interconnect the primary particles, and a uniform carbon coating on each primary particle - and state this is the first report of a micro-sized C-LiMn0.5Fe0.5PO4 with high capacity and high tap density.

Paper_Title: Fabrication of high tap density LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres by a double carbon coating-spray drying method for high rate lithium ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres (double carbon coating + spray drying)
Synthesis_Method: Double carbon coating (ball-milling + pre-sintering) followed by spray drying at 180 C and sintering
Remarks: Main sample. Reversible capacity 160.2 mAh/g at 0.1C over 2.0-4.35 V. Tap density 1.4 g/cm3 (vs 0.82 g/cm3 for the nanoparticle counterpart), carbon 3.26 wt%, conductivity 9.4e-3 S/cm, BET 23.7 m2/g with a main pore size distribution at 30 nm. Volume energy density 801.5 Wh/L at 0.1C, nearly 1.4 times the 482.3 Wh/L of the nano-sized counterpart. Li+ diffusion coefficients from Randles-Sevcik analysis of CVs are 1e-12 to 1e-13 cm2/s, close to literature values, indicating the several-micrometre sphere diameter has little effect on Li+ diffusion from electrolyte into electrode. Pores are ascribed to decomposition and partial oxidation of sucrose from 180 C upward, releasing CO2, CO and furfural-based gases.

Paper_Title: Fabrication of high tap density LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres by a double carbon coating-spray drying method for high rate lithium ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C nanoparticles (vacuum-dried control, no spray drying)
Synthesis_Method: Conventional solid state route: ball-milling, vacuum drying and sintering (no spray drying)
Remarks: Nanoparticle control prepared by vacuum-drying part of the same ball-milled slurry and annealing under identical conditions. Discharge capacity 163.7 mAh/g at 0.1C, marginally above the 160.2 mAh/g of the microspheres, but tap density is only 0.82 g/cm3 and volume energy density only 482.3 Wh/L. Carbon 3.37 wt%, conductivity 1.8e-2 S/cm (the difference from the microspheres is within experimental accuracy). The irregular morphology and aggregation are detrimental to electrode preparation and volume energy density.

Paper_Title: Fabrication of high tap density LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres by a double carbon coating-spray drying method for high rate lithium ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres (double carbon coating + spray drying)
Remarks: Rate ladder for the microspheres from 0.1C to 20C: 150, 145, 138, 133, 129 and 126 mAh/g are quoted with capacity retentions of 94, 91, 87, 83 and 81% at 0.5C, 1C, 3C, 5C and 10C respectively (versus 0.2C); the text lists six capacities against five rates, so the mapping of the final value is ambiguous in the source. Values entered here are 1C = 145 mAh/g and 5C = 133 mAh/g. The remarkable rate performance is attributed to the uniform carbon coating and the hierarchical porous spherical structure: nano-sized primary crystallites shorten the Li+ diffusion path while open mesopores let electrolyte penetrate deep into each micro-sized particle.

Paper_Title: Fabrication of high tap density LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres by a double carbon coating-spray drying method for high rate lithium ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres (double carbon coating + spray drying)
Remarks: At an extremely high current of 20C (3200 mA/g) the micro-sized spheres still delivered 106.3 mAh/g (the conclusions quote 106.4 mAh/g), similar to the 126.0 mAh/g of the nanoparticles. The volume energy density of the microspheres remained 1.3 times higher than that of the nanoparticles even at 20C. No 20C column exists in this dataset, so the value is recorded in remarks only.
Evidence: Fig. 6c-d, Fig. S2, Table S2 (20C, microspheres)

Paper_Title: Fabrication of high tap density LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres by a double carbon coating-spray drying method for high rate lithium ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C nanoparticles (vacuum-dried control, no spray drying)
Synthesis_Method: Conventional solid state route: ball-milling, vacuum drying and sintering (no spray drying)
Remarks: Nanoparticle counterpart discharged 126.0 mAh/g at 20C, higher than the 106.3 mAh/g of the microspheres on a gravimetric basis, but its low packing density means the microspheres still win by 1.3 times on volumetric energy density at this rate. No 20C column exists in this dataset, so the value is recorded in remarks only.

Paper_Title: Fabrication of high tap density LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres by a double carbon coating-spray drying method for high rate lithium ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres (double carbon coating + spray drying)
Remarks: Room-temperature cycling between 4.35 and 2.0 V for 100 cycles at 2C: the composite electrode delivered 138.3 mAh/g and an energy density of 473.5 Wh/kg with 99.1% capacity retention and 98.8% energy density retention.

Paper_Title: Fabrication of high tap density LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres by a double carbon coating-spray drying method for high rate lithium ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LiFe0.6Mn0.4PO4/C microspheres (double carbon coating + spray drying)
Remarks: Over a further 200 cycles at 5C (following the 100 cycles at 2C) the microspheres delivered 128.4 mAh/g and 420.8 Wh/kg, maintaining 98.9% capacity retention and 97.9% energy density retention. The abstract summarises the combined test as 98.9% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 2C and 200 cycles at 5C.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.75Fe0.25PO4/C microspheres using a microwave-assisted process with a complexing agent for high-rate lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Microwave-assisted hydrothermal synthesis with citric acid complexing agent (200 C, 200 W, 15 min) followed by sucrose carbon coating and sintering
Remarks: Best sample of the pH series and the headline material of the paper. Charge and discharge capacities at 0.05C and 25 C were 168 and 163 mAh/g, i.e. 95.3% of theoretical, with a coulombic efficiency of about 97%. Volumetric capacity at 0.05C is 262 mAh/cm3 on a tap density of 1.3 g/cm3 (versus 0.3-0.8 g/cm3 typical of nanoparticles). Lattice constants a = 10.42 A, b = 6.08 A, c = 4.73 A, V = 299.70 A3, matching phase-pure LiMn0.75Fe0.25PO4 and confirming a LiMnPO4-LiFePO4 solid solution. BET 23.2 m2/g, type IV isotherm with H2 hysteresis, mean pore size 3.8 nm, cumulative desorption pore volume 0.06 cm3/g. HR-TEM shows 0.42 nm (101) lattice fringes. ICP-OES gave Li/P 1.00, Mn/P 0.75, Fe/P 0.25. CV at 0.025 mV/s shows peak pairs at 4.15/3.97 V and 3.56/3.50 V, and CV shape is retained up to 1 mV/s. Microwave synthesis: 100 ml Teflon vessel, MARS-5, heated to 200 C at 200 W and held 15 min with stirring; Li:(Mn+Fe):P = 3:1:1.
Evidence: Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Table 1, Fig. S5 (LMFP3, 0.05C at 25 C)

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.75Fe0.25PO4/C microspheres using a microwave-assisted process with a complexing agent for high-rate lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Microwave-assisted hydrothermal synthesis with citric acid complexing agent (200 C, 200 W, 15 min) followed by sucrose carbon coating and sintering
Remarks: At 60 C and 0.05C, LMFP3 showed the highest discharge capacity of the pH series, 170 mAh/g, corresponding to 99.4% of the theoretical capacity. Attributed to the low antisite defect concentration and the porous structure, which lets electrolyte be absorbed into the inner parts of the microspheres. Cells were charged at 0.05C to 4.5 V, held at 4.5 V until the current fell to 0.01C, then discharged at 0.05C to 2.0 V.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.75Fe0.25PO4/C microspheres using a microwave-assisted process with a complexing agent for high-rate lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Microwave-assisted hydrothermal synthesis with citric acid complexing agent (200 C, 200 W, 15 min) followed by sucrose carbon coating and sintering
Remarks: Lowest-pH precursor in the series. Citric acid is only partially ionised at low pH ([C6H7O7]- / [C6H6O7]2-), so free metal ions remain in solution, nuclei form randomly and only partially bond to citrate, and self-assembly yields irregular secondary particles. Discharge capacity 129 mAh/g at 0.05C and 60 C. FTIR symmetric stretching band at 995 cm-1 and Li/P atomic ratio of 0.90 indicate the highest M(Li) antisite defect concentration of the series, which blocks the Li+ migration channel and depresses capacity.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.75Fe0.25PO4/C microspheres using a microwave-assisted process with a complexing agent for high-rate lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Microwave-assisted hydrothermal synthesis with citric acid complexing agent (200 C, 200 W, 15 min) followed by sucrose carbon coating and sintering
Remarks: Intermediate pH sample. Discharge capacity 153 mAh/g at 0.05C and 60 C. FTIR band at 989 cm-1 and Li/P atomic ratio 0.97, i.e. an antisite defect concentration between LMFP1 and LMFP3. The blue shift of the ~980 cm-1 symmetric stretching band from 995 to 983 cm-1 across LMFP1 to LMFP3 tracks the falling antisite defect concentration as precursor pH rises.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.75Fe0.25PO4/C microspheres using a microwave-assisted process with a complexing agent for high-rate lithium ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LiMn0.75Fe0.25PO4/C, LMFP4 (precursor pH 7.89, contains Li3PO4 impurity)
Synthesis_Method: Microwave-assisted hydrothermal synthesis with citric acid complexing agent (200 C, 200 W, 15 min) followed by sucrose carbon coating and sintering
Remarks: Weakly basic precursor. Morphology is perfectly spherical, but XRD shows Li3PO4 impurity peaks because the solubility of Li3PO4 in basic solution is very low, and Li3PO4 is reported to severely degrade electrochemical performance. Discharge capacity is therefore only 109 mAh/g at 0.05C and 60 C despite the ideal morphology, and the Li/P ratio is inflated to 1.03 by the impurity. This makes weakly acidic pH 6.35 the optimum rather than the highest pH tested.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.75Fe0.25PO4/C microspheres using a microwave-assisted process with a complexing agent for high-rate lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Microwave-assisted hydrothermal synthesis with citric acid complexing agent (200 C, 200 W, 15 min) followed by sucrose carbon coating and sintering
Remarks: Rate capability measured in a half cell between 2.0 and 4.5 V at 25 C, with charge and discharge performed at the same C-rate from 0.05C to 60C. At the extremely high 60C rate the cell still delivered about 100 mAh/g, which is 57% of the 0.05C specific capacity, at a coulombic efficiency of about 90%. Attributed to the uniform carbon coating reducing charge transfer resistance and the porous spherical structure allowing deep electrolyte penetration into the secondary particles. This dataset has no 60C column, so the value is recorded in remarks only.
Evidence: Fig. 6c, Fig. S6, Fig. S7 (rate capability, LMFP3)

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.75Fe0.25PO4/C microspheres using a microwave-assisted process with a complexing agent for high-rate lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Microwave-assisted hydrothermal synthesis with citric acid complexing agent (200 C, 200 W, 15 min) followed by sucrose carbon coating and sintering
Remarks: Cycling at 1C and 25 C for 100 cycles: initial discharge capacity 152 mAh/g falling only to 151 mAh/g, i.e. 99.3% capacity retention, with coulombic efficiency remaining at about 96%. The authors attribute the overall performance to the porous spherical structure, the uniform carbon coating layer and the reduced antisite defect concentration achieved by controlling precursor pH.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation
Remarks: MnSO4.H2O and FeSO4.7H2O dissolved together in distilled water at a Mn:Fe cationic ratio of 4:1 with total metal sulfate concentration 0.8 mol/L; 800 mL of 0.6 mol/L H2C2O4 slowly dripped into 500 mL of the sulfate solution while 0.3 mol/L NH4OH held the pH at 3; stirred at 600 rpm and 30 C for 24 h, aged 12 h, filtered, washed and vacuum dried at 80 C for 24 h. ICP gives a Mn:Fe ratio of 0.807:0.193 (0.6% error) against the 0.8:0.2 target. Whole-pattern fitting gives a = 12.005(6) A, b = 5.626(4) A, c = 9.952(5) A.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Remarks: Reported lattice parameters of the iron end member quoted for comparison: a = 11.998 A, b = 5.546 A, c = 9.900 A (Deyrieux, Berro and Peneloux, Bull. Soc. Chim. Fr. 1973, 25).

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Remarks: Reported lattice parameters of the manganese end member quoted for comparison: a = 12.016 A, b = 5.632 A, c = 9.961 A (Angermann and Topfer, J. Mater. Sci. 43 (2008) 5123). The precursor parameters lie between the two end members and closer to the Mn end member, implying homogeneous mixing of the transition metals at the target ratio.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: 18.18 g of the Mn0.8Fe0.2(C2O4).2H2O precursor mixed with 3.72 g Li2CO3 and 11.74 g NH4H2PO4 (molar ratio 2:1:2) plus 4 g glucose as organic additive; milled in a 500 mL steel jar with steel balls of mixed diameters at 400 rpm for 6 h at a ball-to-material weight ratio of 6:1; then heated at 600 C for 10 h under Ar flow. XRD matches the olivine structure of LiMnPO4 and LiFePO4 with cell parameters between the two end members. Table 2 lists a = 6.071 A, b = 10.410 A, c = 4.722 A while the running text quotes a = 6.079(4) A, b = 10.414(6) A, c = 4.728(4) A; both sets appear in the paper and the discrepancy is unresolved.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Remarks: Reported olivine cell parameters quoted for comparison: a = 6.008 A, b = 10.324 A, c = 4.694 A (Padhi, Nanjundaswamy and Goodenough, J. Electrochem. Soc. 144 (1997) 1188).

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Remarks: Reported olivine cell parameters quoted for comparison: a = 6.108 A, b = 10.455 A, c = 4.750 A (Delacourt et al., Solid State Ionics 173 (2004) 113).

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: SEM shows small, homogeneous agglomerated particles in the micrometer range; TEM gives a primary particle size of about 30-50 nm (the average size field records the midpoint of this reported range).

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: HRTEM shows a carbon layer with a typical thickness of 2-3 nm on the particle edges. Two sets of lattice fringes with spacings of 0.52 nm and 0.43 nm agree with the interplanar spacings of the (020) and (011) planes calculated from XRD. The pyrolytic carbon both hinders crystal growth, providing a short pathway for lithium-ion diffusion, and provides a conductive surface layer for electron transfer.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Carbon content 6.8 +/- 0.1 wt% measured by carbon-sulfur determinator (ELTRA CS-800); tap density 0.87 +/- 0.02 g/cm3 by densitometer (KDM01). Electronic conductivity by four-point d.c. probe is 5.8e-4 S/cm for LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C, 10^7 times larger than the 4.3e-11 S/cm of uncoated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4. The carbon content is deliberately lower than the >10 wt% used by Martha et al., which the authors note decreases volumetric specific capacity.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Discharge curves from C/10 to 10C, all samples charged at the same C/10 specific current for identical initial conditions. Two distinct plateaus at approximately 3.55 V and 4.15 V correspond to the Fe2+/Fe3+ and Mn2+/Mn3+ redox couples. A sloped line in the Fe2+/Fe3+ region indicates a solid-solution phase transformation mechanism, while the large flat 4.15 V plateau originates from two-phase equilibrium between fully lithiated LiMnPO4 and fully delithiated MnPO4, consistent with Yamada's LixMnyFe1-yPO4 phase diagram.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Initial discharge capacity of 151.1 mAh/g at 0.1 C between 2.5 and 4.5 V. Excluding the 6.8% coated carbon, the capacity of the active LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 alone would be 162.1 mAh/g at 0.1 C, comparable with the results of S. K. Martha et al.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Discharge capacity of 149.2 mAh/g at 0.2 C.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Discharge capacity of 143.3 mAh/g at 0.5 C.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Discharge capacity of 137.6 mAh/g at 1 C.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Discharge capacity of 125.8 mAh/g at 2 C.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Discharge capacity of 98.4 mAh/g at 5 C.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Discharge capacity of 82 mAh/g at 10 C, the headline high-rate figure of the paper. Excluding the 6.8% coated carbon the active-material capacity would be 88 mAh/g at 10 C. The high capacity and impressive rate performance are attributed to the homogeneous distribution of the transition-metal elements and the effective carbon coating.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Cycling protocol: 5 cycles each at 0.1 and 0.2 C, 10 cycles each at 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 10 C, then back to 0.1 C for the last 5 cycles. The cell is stable at every rate and the discharge capacity decreased by only about 3 mAh/g when the current returned to 0.1 C after 60 cycles at different rates; the abstract quotes 148 mAh/g for the 60th cycle.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: CV at 0.05 mV/s over 2.5-4.8 V at room temperature: redox activity of both couples with peak potentials around 3.64/3.51 V for Fe2+/Fe3+ and 4.23/3.89 V for Mn2+/Mn3+, at the expected 4:1 ratio of the charges involved. Relative to LiFePO4/C the Fe oxidation peak shifts only slightly lower (3.67 to 3.64 V) while the reduction peak shifts significantly higher (3.18 to 3.51 V), implying the Fe redox couple is more reversible in LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C and that the presence of Mn2+ affects the Fe charge-discharge reactions.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Remarks: Commercial LiFePO4/C reference containing 3.0% carbon with a particle size of about 100 nm. CV at 0.05 mV/s over 2.5-4.5 V shows anodic and cathodic peaks at 3.67 and 3.18 V for the Fe2+/Fe3+ couple, a peak separation of 0.49 V.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Remarks: Reference LiFePO4/C measured under identical testing conditions: specific capacity 163.0 mAh/g at 0.1 C.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Remarks: Reference LiFePO4/C: 143.1 mAh/g at 1 C, with an energy density of 450 Wh/kg at the same rate.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Remarks: Reference LiFePO4/C: 107.5 mAh/g at 5 C, with an energy density of 308 Wh/kg.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Remarks: Reference LiFePO4/C: 87.2 mAh/g at 10 C.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Energy density comparison under identical testing conditions: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C delivers 483.9 Wh/kg at 1 C versus 450 Wh/kg for LiFePO4/C, and 329.6 Wh/kg at 5 C versus 308 Wh/kg. Energy density is around 10% higher than LiFePO4/C despite the higher carbon content (6.8% versus 3.0%), coming mainly from the higher average discharge voltage of about 4 V, roughly 0.6 V above LiFePO4/C.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Positive electrode: 80% LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C, 10% acetylene black (TIMCAL, >99%) and 10% PVDF, with 4.5 mg/cm2 of active material on the disk electrode. Metallic lithium foil counter electrode, Celgard 2300 separator, 1 M LiPF6 in EC+DMC (1:1 by volume); cells assembled in a glove box with H2O and O2 both below 1 ppm; charge-discharge between 2.5 and 4.5 V on a Land CT2001A tester.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Background values quoted: theoretical energy density of LiMnPO4 is 697 Wh/kg against 586 Wh/kg for LiFePO4; the Mn3+/Mn2+ redox potential of 4.1 V vs Li/Li+ is about 20% higher than the Fe3+/Fe2+ couple; electronic conductivity of LiMnPO4 is below 1e-10 S/cm against 1.8e-9 S/cm for LiFePO4. Synthesis temperature of Mn-rich LiFe1-xMnxPO4 is normally chosen between 550 and 650 C for crystal stability, at which Mn and Fe may not be homogeneous enough.

Paper_Title: Synthesis of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C by co-precipitation method and its electrochemical performances as a cathode material for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Co-precipitation precursor + ball milling + calcination
Remarks: Conclusion: the nanometer LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 particles of 30-50 nm with a 2-3 nm carbon coating and a low carbon content of 6.8 wt% gave 151.1 mAh/g at 0.1 C and 82 mAh/g at 10 C, with better cycling ability and higher energy density than LiFePO4/C, ascribed to the small active-particle size, the carbon coating and the homogeneity of transition-metal distribution.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Sol-gel route: citric acid, Mn(CH3COO)2.4H2O, FeC2O4.2H2O, LiCH3COO.2H2O and NH4H2PO4 in a mole ratio of 1.20:0.80:0.20:1.05:1.00 with ethylene glycol dissolved in 1.0 M HCl; 20 wt% acetylene black (Nippon Carbon, special type for Li-ion batteries) added and a black gel formed on heating at 90 C; gel heated at 400 C for 5 h then 800 C for 15 h under Ar/H2 (8%). The AB loading follows the optimized value of Sun et al. for a carbon-LiMnPO4 composite. XRD shows sharp peaks, no impurity phase, and a residual AB feature confirming the added acetylene black survives the 800 C heating. Cell parameters by Jade 5.0: a = 6.0812(3) A, b = 10.4233(6) A, c = 4.7320(4) A, V = 299.94 A^3, consistent with Martha et al.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Control sample prepared by the identical sol-gel route but without adding acetylene black, giving a conventional core-shell structure. XRD pattern similar to the AB-embedded sample with sharp peaks and no impurity phase, indicating a pure LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 solid-solution phase.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Refined unit-cell volume of 299.94 A^3 from a = 6.0812(3), b = 10.4233(6) and c = 4.7320(4) A.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Carbon content estimated by TGA (25 to 800 C at 10 C/min under oxygen) as 33 wt%. The authors note that carbon fully encapsulated inside LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 might escape detection, but consider this unlikely because the phosphate decomposes into Li3PO4 and Fe2O3 during TGA, exposing the embedded AB.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Carbon content estimated by TGA as 16 wt%, roughly half that of the AB-embedded sample, consistent with the absence of the 20 wt% added acetylene black.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: SEM shows a well-distributed micro-nano structure with primary particle size in the range 80-100 nm reunited into secondary particles of 1-2 um (the average size field records the midpoint of the primary range). TEM reveals an embedded structure padded with AB balls of 10-60 nm distributed uniformly through the LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4, completely different from a simple porous structure. Some unfilled pores are visible, attributed to blind or small pores in the AB that the preparation solution did not fill. Growth of the LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 particles is inhibited by the AB so the primary particles are far smaller than in the control.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: SEM morphology similar to the AB-embedded sample, but TEM shows a distinct core-shell structure: particle size about 200 nm with a uniform carbon layer of about 10 nm thickness, similar to material prepared by a common sol-gel method.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: BET specific surface area of 17.9 m2/g, larger than the core-shell control, and the sample retains the pore-size distribution of acetylene black from 50 to 200 nm, confirming the contribution of AB to the porous structure. TEM of the 400 C gel precursor retains the AB morphology, showing AB has been successfully embedded at the precursor stage.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: BET specific surface area of 13.5 m2/g, lower than the AB-embedded sample, with a narrow pore-size distribution peaked around 30-40 nm.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Composition_Formula: Acetylene black (AB, Nippon Carbon, reference material)
Remarks: Acetylene black used as the embedded carbon source: agglomerated particles of 20-40 nm, BET specific surface area 63.4 m2/g, broad pore-size distribution from 20 to 200 nm concentrated in the 20-40 nm range.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Charged at a constant 0.05 C to 4.8 V then discharged to 2.0 V at 0.1 C (1 C = 150 mAh/g in this work): reversible capacity of 160 mAh/g. Two discharge plateaus at about 4.0 V and 3.5 V vs Li+/Li correspond to Mn3+/Mn2+ and Fe3+/Fe2+.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Under the same protocol the core-shell control delivers only 142 mAh/g at 0.1 C, with the same two discharge plateaus at about 4.0 V and 3.5 V.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Reversible capacity of 152 mAh/g at 0.2 C.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery

Remarks: Reversible capacity of 141 mAh/g at 0.5 C.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery

Remarks: Reversible capacity of 128 mAh/g at 1 C.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Reversible capacity of 110 mAh/g at 2 C.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Reversible capacity of 86 mAh/g at 5 C, consistently above the core-shell control at every rate tested.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Reversible capacity of 123 mAh/g at 0.2 C.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery

Remarks: Reversible capacity of 103 mAh/g at 1 C.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery

Remarks: Reversible capacity of 91 mAh/g at 2 C.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Reversible capacity of 69 mAh/g at 5 C.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: After cycling across the full 0.1 to 5 C rate ladder the sample recovers 163 mAh/g at 0.1 C, exceeding its primary capacity and showing the structural stability of the embedded material.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: After the full rate ladder the core-shell control recovers 126 mAh/g at 0.1 C, also without reduction of its primary capacity.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Cyclic performance determined by charging to 4.8 V at 0.1 C and discharging to 2.0 V at 0.05 C: the charge-discharge efficiency stays higher than 95% and the discharge capacity is almost unchanged after 80 cycles, showing good structural stability of the embedded architecture.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: EIS at open-circuit voltage (3.0 V) with 10 mV rms from 1 MHz to 1 mHz. For the fresh cell the AB-embedded sample shows a smaller interface resistance (merged high-frequency semicircle) and a steeper low-frequency line, i.e. faster lithium-ion diffusion, than the core-shell control, ascribed to its porous embedded structure. After 15 cycles the interface resistance falls for both electrodes and the difference between them narrows, but the difference in lithium-ion diffusion kinetics persists, suggesting the internal structure differs and is retained on cycling. Numerical fitted resistances are not reported.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Remarks: Cited comparison: the LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite developed by Hu et al. (Funct. Mater. Lett. 4 (2011) 319) delivers approximately 80 mAh/g at 0.1 C, far below both samples in this work, illustrating that the preparation process strongly governs discharge performance.

Paper_Title: Acetylene black-embedded LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4/C composite as cathode for lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Sol-gel
Remarks: Electrode formulation designed for equivalent comparison: the AB-embedded electrode is active material and PVDF only in a 9:1 weight ratio with no added conductive carbon, whereas the core-shell electrode is active material, acetylene black and PVDF at 7:2:1. The LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 content of both electrodes is about 60 wt% and the loading on both is about 3 mg/cm2, so the comparison can be considered equivalent.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Spray-dry route: aqueous mixture of LiOH.H2O, MnCO3, FeC2O4.2H2O and NH4H2PO4 in a molar ratio of 1:0.8:0.2:1 with 10 wt% glucose, stirred to a slurry of 30 wt% solid content, spray dried at 120 C in air, then calcined at 650 C for 8 h at 5 C/min under Ar. Rietveld refinement (MAUD) gives a = 6.0855 A, b = 10.4234 A, c = 4.7379 A, V = 300.5408 A^3 with Rw = 2.671 and Rb = 1.860.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: The as-prepared LMFP was mixed in PEG 400 under stirring, then 1 M H3PO4 and 1 M LiOH were added dropwise, followed by slow addition of 0.5 M FeSO4; PEG 400 to H3PO4 volume ratio 1:40 and H3PO4:LiOH:FeSO4 molar ratio 1:3:1. The slurry was heated in a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave at 180 C for 12 h, filtered and washed, then mixed with 10 wt% glucose at 30 wt% solids, spray dried at 120 C and calcined at 650 C for 8 h under Ar. Carbon content of the final product about 4.4 wt%. Rietveld refinement gives a = 6.0824 A, c = 4.7361 A, V = 300.2645 A^3 with Rw = 2.287 and Rb = 1.871; Table 1 lists b as 40.4231 A, which is an evident typographical error for 10.4231 A. The slight lattice contraction versus LMFP is attributed to diffusion of smaller Fe2+ into the olivine lattice in place of Mn2+.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: XPS: Fe 2p3/2 binding energy around 710.6 eV with a satellite near 724.1 eV matching Fe2+; Mn 2p1/2 at about 653.9 eV and Mn 2p3/2 at 641.4 eV with a spin-orbit splitting of 5.5 eV. Surface atomic concentrations are Fe 1.45% and Mn 5.53%.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: XPS spectra of Fe 2p and Mn 2p show no significant difference in binding energy from the pristine material, but the surface atomic concentrations shift to Fe 1.67% (higher than LMFP) and Mn 5.40% (lower than LMFP), showing the transition-metal concentration at the surface has been changed by the modification.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: SEM shows microspheres of about 20-30 um composed of agglomerated nanosized primary particles of 40-50 nm diameter (the average size field records the midpoint of the primary-particle range). BET specific surface area 25.93 m2/g.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: Same microsphere morphology of 20-30 um from 40-50 nm primary particles, but with a lower BET specific surface area of 14.2 m2/g after the solvothermal surface treatment and second calcination.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: HRTEM shows the LMFP particle coated by amorphous carbon and well crystallised with a single d-spacing of 1.03 nm, corresponding to the (100) plane of LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 - a uniform solid solution with no surface phase differentiation.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: HRTEM shows three distinct sets of lattice fringes after surface modification: an outer layer with d = 0.23 nm matching the (012) plane of LiFePO4, a sub-surface layer with d = 0.37 nm corresponding to the (101) plane of LiMn1-xFexPO4 with x about 0.29, and an inner layer with d = 0.30 nm associated with the (200) plane of LiMn1-xFexPO4 with x about 0.25. This confirms the surface structure evolved from a uniform solid solution into an Fe-rich phase.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: SEM cross-section of a particle of nearly 15 um diameter with EDXS line scanning shows the concentrations of Fe and Mn are constant from one side to the other, i.e. no concentration gradient in the pristine material.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: SEM cross-section with EDXS line scanning clearly exhibits a concentration gradient: Fe concentration is higher at the particle surface and decreases linearly toward the centre, while Mn concentration is lower at the surface and increases linearly inward, confirming the gradient structure was successfully constructed by the solvothermal treatment.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: First charge/discharge at 0.05 C and room temperature between 2.0 and 4.5 V: initial discharge capacity of 159 mAh/g.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: First charge/discharge at 0.05 C and room temperature: initial discharge capacity of only 144 mAh/g, 15 mAh/g below the concentration-gradient material.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: Rate testing charged at 0.2 C and discharged at 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 and 5.0 C: reversible capacity of 130 mAh/g even at 5 C, the headline rate figure of the paper. The concentration-gradient material shows a much higher capacity than the pristine LMFP under all discharge rates, and the capacity recovers to its initial state on returning to 1 C after the 5 C testing, indicating good reversibility.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Under the same rate protocol the pristine LMFP delivers 116 mAh/g at 5 C, 14 mAh/g below the concentration-gradient material. Capacities at the intermediate 0.2, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0 C rates are shown only graphically.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: Cycling at 1 C and 25 C for 100 cycles: excellent cycling performance with an essentially flat capacity curve throughout. Numerical retention at room temperature is not quoted in the text. Note: the paper writes the C-rate as '1 degrees C' throughout, an evident typographical substitution for 1 C.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Cycling at 1 C and 25 C for 100 cycles: almost no capacity fading was observed at room temperature, running slightly below the concentration-gradient material throughout.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: Cycling at 1 C and an elevated temperature of 55 C: 98% discharge capacity retention after 50 cycles, the headline cycling result of the paper. Attributed to the Fe-rich surface phase resisting electrolyte corrosion and to the gradient preventing segregation at the bulk/outer-layer interface, which maintains the lithium-ion transport channels at the surface.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Cycling at 1 C and 55 C: significant capacity loss with a sudden capacity fading observed after 35 cycles. Attributed to structural transformation at the particle surface from the high reactivity of Mn with the electrolyte, with dissolved Mn depositing on the anode and destroying the SEI, increasing the cathode/electrolyte interface resistance.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: Mn dissolved into the electrolyte during storage at 25 C: 0.37 ppm after 1 week, 14.20 ppm after 2 weeks and 49.28 ppm after 3 weeks - consistently and substantially below the pristine material at every time point.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Mn dissolved into the electrolyte during storage at 25 C: 5.84 ppm after 1 week, 30.95 ppm after 2 weeks and 92.00 ppm after 3 weeks.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: Mn dissolved into the electrolyte during storage at 55 C: 2.14 ppm after 1 week, 251.30 ppm after 2 weeks and 1329 ppm after 3 weeks. The gap against the pristine material is largest after one week, which is linked to the difference in elevated-temperature capacity fading.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Mn dissolved into the electrolyte during storage at 55 C: 15.32 ppm after 1 week, 346.10 ppm after 2 weeks and 1416 ppm after 3 weeks - about seven times the concentration-gradient material after one week of soaking.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: EIS fitted with an Re + R1/CPE1 + R2/CPE2 + W0 equivalent circuit at 1 C full discharge state, 5 mV amplitude after three cycles at 0.1 C: electrolyte resistance Re = 0.76625 ohm, surface-film resistance Rsur = 110.34 ohm and charge-transfer resistance Rct = 263.80 ohm.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: EIS: Re = 0.8405 ohm, Rsur = 50.78 ohm and Rct = 112.10 ohm. Both R1 and R2 are decreased by the surface modification, which the authors attribute to suppression of Mn dissolution protecting the SEI and to the Fe-rich phase preserving the lithium-ion transport channel.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Warburg coefficient sigma taken as the slope of Z' versus omega^-1/2 in the low-frequency region: 44.70 for the pristine material. The lithium-ion diffusion coefficient calculated from D = R^2T^2/(2A^2n^4F^4C^2sigma^2) with A = 1.32665 cm2, n = 1 and C = 6.38e-3 mol/cm3 is about 2.4e-13 cm2/s.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: Warburg coefficient sigma = 20.17, less than half that of the pristine material, giving a lithium-ion diffusion coefficient of about 1.2e-12 cm2/s - five times higher, demonstrating that the surface Fe-rich composition benefits Li+ migration.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: CV at 0.1 mV/s over 2.0-4.5 V shows the oxidation and reduction peaks of Fe3+/Fe2+ and Mn3+/Mn2+. The peak current density for the concentration-gradient material is much higher than for the pristine LMFP, and the anodic-to-cathodic peak separations for both Mn and Fe are smaller, showing the gradient surface layer improves conductivity and weakens polarization. Numerical peak potentials are not quoted.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying
Remarks: Electrode: 80 wt% active material, 15 wt% Super P and 5 wt% PVDF in NMP coated on Al foil and dried at 80 C for 12 h; thickness about 25 um giving a loading density of 2.5-3.5 mg/cm2 (the mass-loading field records the midpoint). 2032 coin cells assembled in an argon glove box with lithium metal anode and Celgard 2502 separator; 1 M LiPF6 in EC:DMC 3:7 by volume; CC-CV protocol over 2.0-4.5 V on a LAND-CT2001A tester.

Paper_Title: Concentration-gradient LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathode material for high performance lithium ion battery
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying + solvothermal surface treatment
Remarks: Conclusion: the concentration-gradient structure takes advantage of anticorrosion by the surface Fe-rich phase and the stability of that surface structure, giving superior cycling performance; the Fe-rich phase also benefits electronic and ionic kinetics, giving excellent rate performance. The design is proposed as a route to minimize the mismatch between surface and bulk phase that limits conventional LiFePO4-coated core-shell architectures, where the 11.6% volume change of the LiMnPO4 core against 6.8% for the LiFePO4 shell opens a void at the core/shell interface on long-term cycling.

Paper_Title: Construction of high performance N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanocrystal cathode for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis in ethylene glycol at 180 C for 18 h, sucrose carbon coating, melamine N-doping, pre-decomposition at 350 C and sintering at 650 C
Remarks: Undoped baseline. Discharge capacity 124.9 mAh/g at 0.1C, the lowest of the series. Carbon 7.11 wt%, electronic conductivity 2.4e-3 S/cm, Rct 402.2 ohm, Li+ diffusion coefficient 1.55e-14 cm2/s. Raman ID/IG 0.81. The under-developed nanosheet crystal structure obstructs Li+ migration. After 200 cycles at 1C the capacity drops to 99.3 mAh/g, an 88.34% retention, and ex-situ XRD shows weakened peak intensity, i.e. declining crystallinity. Mn2+ and Fe2+ dissolved into electrolyte over 15 days of immersion: 5.33 and 0.302 ppm. BJH pore size distribution spans 2-50 nm with the maximum adsorption volume at 4 nm.

Paper_Title: Construction of high performance N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanocrystal cathode for lithium-ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LMFP-3: N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 (N:C atomic ratio 3:100)
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis in ethylene glycol at 180 C for 18 h, sucrose carbon coating, melamine N-doping, pre-decomposition at 350 C and sintering at 650 C
Remarks: Lowest melamine loading. Discharge capacity 133.8 mAh/g at 0.1C, carbon 6.92 wt%, conductivity 6.3e-3 S/cm, Rct 161.1 ohm, D(Li+) 3.29e-14 cm2/s. Dopant molar ratio column records the nominal N:C atomic ratio of 3:100 as 0.03.

Paper_Title: Construction of high performance N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanocrystal cathode for lithium-ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LMFP-5: N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 (N:C atomic ratio 5:100)
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis in ethylene glycol at 180 C for 18 h, sucrose carbon coating, melamine N-doping, pre-decomposition at 350 C and sintering at 650 C
Remarks: Intermediate melamine loading. Discharge capacity 139.7 mAh/g at 0.1C, carbon 7.05 wt%, conductivity 8.6e-3 S/cm, Rct 105.0 ohm, D(Li+) 7.56e-14 cm2/s. Dopant molar ratio column records the nominal N:C atomic ratio of 5:100 as 0.05.

Paper_Title: Construction of high performance N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanocrystal cathode for lithium-ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LMFP-7: N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 (N:C atomic ratio 7:100) - optimum
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis in ethylene glycol at 180 C for 18 h, sucrose carbon coating, melamine N-doping, pre-decomposition at 350 C and sintering at 650 C
Remarks: Best sample of the series: 154.7, 144.2 and 110.0 mAh/g at 0.1, 1 and 5C, with two flat plateaus at 3.6 and 4.1 V. Carbon 7.02 wt%, highest electronic conductivity of the series at 1.1e-2 S/cm, lowest charge-transfer resistance 46.9 ohm and highest Li+ diffusion coefficient 1.35e-13 cm2/s. Raman ID/IG 0.86, higher than the 0.81 of LMFP-0, indicating more defects after N doping. XPS N 1s deconvolutes into pyridinic (32.3%), pyrrolic (39.4%) and graphitic N (28.3%), so pyridinic plus pyrrolic reaches 71.4%; these edge sites raise electrode-electrolyte wettability and cut interfacial resistance, while graphitic N adds electrons to the delocalised pi system. The minimised b parameter shortens the b-axis Li+ migration path. CV redox pairs show the smallest potential differences of the series, 0.325 V (Mn) and 0.111 V (Fe). Mn2+ and Fe2+ dissolution after 15 days is only 2.83 and 0.227 ppm against 5.33 and 0.302 ppm for LMFP-0. Excess doping is counterproductive - see LMFP-9.

Paper_Title: Construction of high performance N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanocrystal cathode for lithium-ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LMFP-9: N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 (N:C atomic ratio 9:100) - over-doped
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis in ethylene glycol at 180 C for 18 h, sucrose carbon coating, melamine N-doping, pre-decomposition at 350 C and sintering at 650 C
Remarks: Over-doped sample showing the turning point of the trend. Capacity falls back to 148.6 mAh/g at 0.1C and drops sharply at high rate, conductivity declines to 9.1e-3 S/cm, Rct rises to 110.7 ohm and the Li+ diffusion coefficient collapses to 6.86e-15 cm2/s - the lowest of the series, below even the undoped LMFP-0. Two causes are given: the b parameter grows back to 10.4521 A, lengthening the Li+ migration path, and the 200 nm particles slow insertion and extraction. Mechanistically, an excessive proportion of defective N atoms induces quantum interference effects and the defects act as scattering centres that increase localisation and reduce overall electronic conductivity.

Paper_Title: Construction of high performance N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanocrystal cathode for lithium-ion batteries
Composition_Formula: LMFP-7: N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 (N:C atomic ratio 7:100)
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis in ethylene glycol at 180 C for 18 h, sucrose carbon coating, melamine N-doping, pre-decomposition at 350 C and sintering at 650 C
Remarks: Cycling at 1C charge and 1C discharge for 200 cycles: capacity falls only to 131.8 mAh/g, a 93.81% retention, with coulombic efficiency close to 100% and the charge-discharge plateaus well maintained. Ex-situ XRD of the cathode film after 200 cycles shows no new phases and no significant peak shift, and the main peak intensity is preserved, confirming structural stability.

Paper_Title: Construction of high performance N-doped carbon coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 nanocrystal cathode for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis in ethylene glycol at 180 C for 18 h, sucrose carbon coating, melamine N-doping, pre-decomposition at 350 C and sintering at 650 C
Remarks: Undoped control under the same 1C/1C protocol: capacity drops to 99.3 mAh/g after 200 cycles, an 88.34% retention, and the charge-discharge profiles deteriorate obviously. Ex-situ XRD shows evidently weakened peak intensity, i.e. decreasing crystallinity and gradual structural degradation.

Paper_Title: Insights on the delithiation/lithiation reactions of LixMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 mesocrystals in Li+ batteries by in situ techniques
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis in DMF at 180 C for 12 h followed by sucrose impregnation and calcination at 700 C for 3 h
Remarks: Model compound for the kinetic study. Capacity 133 mAh/g at 0.05C, about 78% of the 171 mAh/g theoretical value (1C = 171 mA/g), and 70 mAh/g at 10C, i.e. 53% of the 0.05C value. Carbon content 5.2 wt% by CHNS; Mn/Fe atomic ratio ~4 by ICP-AES; EDS mapping confirms homogeneous Mn, Fe, P and O distribution. CV at 0.01 mV/s gives anodic peaks at 3.59 and 4.15 V and cathodic peaks at 3.99 and 3.55 V, and the CV shape is retained up to 0.2 mV/s. The Mn redox response is asymmetric, the reduction peak current being higher, which reflects innately more sluggish charging than discharging kinetics. The high rate capability is credited to the porous mesocrystal architecture of ~40 nm crystallites plus conformal carbon on each nanoparticle.

Paper_Title: Insights on the delithiation/lithiation reactions of LixMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 mesocrystals in Li+ batteries by in situ techniques
Composition_Formula: Carbon-coated LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 mesocrystals - operando XRD phase behaviour
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis in DMF at 180 C for 12 h followed by sucrose impregnation and calcination at 700 C for 3 h
Remarks: Operando XRD at C/20 through a transmission window in a 2032 cell. Delithiation begins as a solid solution within the Fe2+/Fe3+ region (1 >= x >= ~0.8 in LixMn0.8Fe0.2PO4), shown by continuous peak shift with the a and b axes shrinking and c elongating. Further delithiation (~0.8 >= x >= ~0.2) produces new Mn0.8Fe0.2PO4 (alpha phase) peaks, i.e. a first-order two-phase reaction accompanying Mn2+ oxidation at ~4.1 V. Discharge reverses the alpha-to-beta evolution, but a small amount of alpha phase persists at full discharge, so Mn3+ reduction is incomplete and the insertion and extraction pathways differ. dQ/dV peaks at ~3.55 V confirm a distinct beta-prime intermediate phase, and peaks at ~4.11 V correspond to beta-prime and alpha coexistence. This row carries no capacity value because it records structural rather than rate data.

Gradual voltage slope from ~4.4 to 3.3 V. Fell to 85.3% of initial energy density after 100 cycles at C/3 - the worst retention in the study - with impedance rising sharply from a kinetically limiting reduced surface layer formed by cycling to the 4.4 V upper cutoff.

Paper_Title: Practical Pathways to Higher Energy Density LMFP Battery Cathodes
Composition_Formula: Blend cathode: 70 wt% LMFP60 (LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4) + 30 wt% NMC811
Synthesis_Method: Commercially procured active materials (Gelon LIB, ALEEES, Li-FUN); electrodes made in-house by slurry mixing (THINKY ARE-250) and casting (ERICHSEN COATMASTER 510)
Remarks: Blend row. 173 mAh/g, 635 Wh/kg and 1389 Wh/L (digitised from Fig. 4), between the two constituents (LMFP60 142, NMC811 213 mAh/g). Average discharge voltage 3.67 V vs 3.64 V for LMFP60, which with the extra capacity gives a 23% gravimetric and 50% volumetric energy density gain over LMFP60 alone; the bimodal packing raised electrode density to 2.4 g/cm3. The voltage profile shows features of both constituents (>4 V activity from NMC, 3.9 V plateau from LMFP) and its more gradual slope with SOC is useful for OCV-based state-of-charge estimation. Retention 87.7% of initial energy after 100 cycles, between the unblended variants; the blend tracked NMC811 for the first 55 cycles then deviated, and by cycle 100 had lost most of its NMC-like character and followed the LMFP60 curve.

Paper_Title: Providing high stability to suppress metal dissolution in LiMn0.5Fe0.5PO4 cathode materials by Zn doping
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal (180 C, 15 h) followed by carbon-coating calcination
Remarks: Lattice a = 10.3885, b = 6.0566, c = 4.7311 A. Warburg factor sigma = 13.85. 1C = 150 mA/g. Undoped baseline. HR-TEM after 100 cycles at 2C shows particle destruction and the (200) spacing falling irreversibly from 5.16 to 5.08 A, i.e. the lattice volume is not recovered on discharge because Fe or Mn has dissolved. XPS on the cycled separator shows a contaminated surface with strong C 1s, F 1s and O 1s signals plus clear Fe2+/Fe3+ and Mn multiplet peaks, together with Li-F at 685.67 eV from LiPF6 decomposition.

Paper_Title: Providing high stability to suppress metal dissolution in LiMn0.5Fe0.5PO4 cathode materials by Zn doping
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal (180 C, 15 h) followed by carbon-coating calcination
Remarks: Lattice a = 10.3926, b = 6.0584, c = 4.7319 A. Warburg factor sigma = 11.08. 1C = 150 mA/g. Light doping already improves capacity over the undoped baseline and cuts Rct more than fourfold, but rate capability at high C-rates remains poor relative to the 1.0% sample.

Paper_Title: Providing high stability to suppress metal dissolution in LiMn0.5Fe0.5PO4 cathode materials by Zn doping
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal (180 C, 15 h) followed by carbon-coating calcination
Remarks: Lattice a = 10.3926, b = 6.0616, c = 4.7329 A. Warburg factor sigma = 10.11. 1C = 150 mA/g. Optimum doping level and the best sample of the study on every metric: highest capacity at all C-rates including 95.3 mAh/g at 5C, lowest Rct, highest Li+ diffusion coefficient and the smallest CV voltage gap between oxidation and reduction. Zn2+ has an ionic radius close to Mn2+ at 6-coordination, so it substitutes on the transition-metal site and widens the interplanar spacing (the (111) peak shifts left) without disturbing the olivine structure, giving larger Li+ transport channels. Post-mortem HR-TEM shows only minor particle destruction and the (200) spacing nearly recovered, 5.18 -> 5.14 A: Zn acts as a structural pillar limiting volume change. The cycled separator is visibly clean and its XPS shows only separator carbon with no electrolyte-derived species, confirming suppressed Fe and Mn dissolution. Oxidation peaks 3.54-3.56 V (Fe2+/Fe3+) and 4.15-4.17 V (Mn2+/Mn3+); reduction 3.40-3.44 and 3.98-4.02 V.

Paper_Title: Providing high stability to suppress metal dissolution in LiMn0.5Fe0.5PO4 cathode materials by Zn doping
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal (180 C, 15 h) followed by carbon-coating calcination
Remarks: Lattice a = 10.3943, b = 6.0605, c = 4.7362 A. Warburg factor sigma = 13.37. 1C = 150 mA/g. Over-doped. Gave the lowest discharge capacities of all four samples at every C-rate and the poorest cycling among the doped series, showing that 2% Zn is an excessive substitution level; Rct and the Warburg factor both rise again relative to 1.0% Zn.

Paper_Title: Providing high stability to suppress metal dissolution in LiMn0.5Fe0.5PO4 cathode materials by Zn doping
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal (180 C, 15 h) followed by carbon-coating calcination
Remarks: Initial 2C discharge capacity 110.18 mAh/g falling to 96.87 mAh/g after 100 cycles. Cycling at 2C for 100 cycles; the 1.0% Zn sample gives the highest retention of the series and the undoped baseline the lowest, the trend the paper attributes directly to suppressed metal dissolution.

Paper_Title: Providing high stability to suppress metal dissolution in LiMn0.5Fe0.5PO4 cathode materials by Zn doping
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal (180 C, 15 h) followed by carbon-coating calcination
Remarks: Numerical initial and final 2C capacities are not tabulated for this composition; only the retention figure is reported. Cycling at 2C for 100 cycles; the 1.0% Zn sample gives the highest retention of the series and the undoped baseline the lowest, the trend the paper attributes directly to suppressed metal dissolution.

Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal (180 C, 15 h) followed by carbon-coating calcination
Remarks: Initial 2C discharge capacity 126.19 mAh/g falling to 116.88 mAh/g after 100 cycles. Cycling at 2C for 100 cycles; the 1.0% Zn sample gives the highest retention of the series and the undoped baseline the lowest, the trend the paper attributes directly to suppressed metal dissolution.

Paper_Title: Constructing durable carbon layer on LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with superior long-term cycling performance for lithium-ion battery
Composition_Formula: C-LMFP: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with an additional CVD carbon layer (H2/C2H2, 650 C, 8 min)
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying then calcination, followed by chemical vapour deposition (CVD) of a second carbon layer from H2/C2H2 at 650 C for 8 min (flow 15 and 20 cm3/min)
Remarks: CVD-coated sample, the optimised material of the paper. Two carbon layers are visible in HRTEM: an inner organic-derived layer and a ~2 nm outer CVD layer; d(111) = 0.35 nm. Raman ID/IG falls to 0.8097 from 0.8459 for the untreated sample, i.e. a higher graphitisation degree. Retains 95% of capacity after 450 cycles at 1C at room temperature (96% is quoted in the abstract for the same test). Rct entered as 11.21 ohm after 50 cycles and 16.67 ohm after 300 cycles; RSEI grows only marginally, 13.69 -> 20.03 ohm, versus more than a doubling for the untreated sample. Mn dissolved into the electrolyte 1.25 ppm at 25 C.

Paper_Title: Constructing durable carbon layer on LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with superior long-term cycling performance for lithium-ion battery
Composition_Formula: LMFP: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 control, conventional glucose-derived carbon only (no CVD)
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying of the aqueous precursor slurry followed by calcination at 650 C for 8 h in Ar (no CVD step)
Remarks: Untreated control. Carbon layer measured at about 25 nm with d(001) = 0.47 nm; Raman ID/IG = 0.8459. Lost almost 20% of initial capacity after 320 cycles at 1C at room temperature (retention entered as 80%), with capacity fade clearly visible from about cycle 200. RSEI more than doubles across 300 cycles, 16.66 -> 41.08 ohm, attributed to Mn2+ deposition altering the anode SEI; Rs also rises from 1.548 to 6.005 ohm. Mn dissolved into the electrolyte 2.84 ppm at 25 C, more than double the CVD-coated sample.

Paper_Title: Constructing durable carbon layer on LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with superior long-term cycling performance for lithium-ion battery
Composition_Formula: C-LMFP: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with an additional CVD carbon layer, tested at 55 C
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying then calcination, followed by CVD carbon coating from H2/C2H2 at 650 C
Remarks: Elevated-temperature cycling at 1C. Retains 97% of capacity after 50 cycles at 55 C. Mn dissolved into the electrolyte 4.87 ppm at 55 C versus 10.59 ppm for the untreated sample - the direct evidence that the CVD carbon layer shields the particles from HF attack and electrolyte corrosion.

Paper_Title: Constructing durable carbon layer on LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with superior long-term cycling performance for lithium-ion battery
Composition_Formula: LMFP: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 control (no CVD), tested at 55 C
Synthesis_Method: Spray drying then calcination at 650 C for 8 h in Ar (no CVD step)
Remarks: Elevated-temperature cycling at 1C. Capacity fade is clearly visible from about cycle 25 and roughly 10% of capacity is lost by cycle 50 (retention entered as 89%). Mn dissolved into the electrolyte 10.59 ppm at 55 C, nearly four times the room-temperature value, confirming that Mn3+ disproportionation and dissolution is the dominant fade mechanism at elevated temperature.

Paper_Title: Iron-assisted carbon coating strategy for improved electrochemical LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathodes
Composition_Formula: LMFP/Fe/C: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with iron-catalysed graphitised carbon coating
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis (240 C, 4 h) followed by sequential coating with iron oxalate then glucose and calcination at 650 C, so that Fe formed in situ catalyses graphitisation of the carbon
Remarks: Iron-catalysed coating, the optimised material. Discharge capacities 152.3 / 141.9 / 132.1 / 105.6 / 76.0 mAh/g at 0.2 / 0.5 / 1 / 5 / 10C (1C = 170 mA/g); the 0.2C, 0.5C and 10C values fall outside the dataset columns. Graphitised carbon layer is uniform and only 2.2 nm thick and sits almost entirely on the particle surfaces because there is no Fe outside the particles; Raman IG/ID = 1.20. Rct 34.26 ohm and Rs 8.52 ohm measured at full charge after 30 cycles at 0.2C (Warburg factor 37.76). CV peak separation for Fe2+/Fe3+ is 0.18 V at 0.1 mV/s versus 0.42 V for the uncatalysed control, and for Mn2+/Mn3+ 0.42 V versus 0.68 V, indicating markedly better reversibility.

Paper_Title: Iron-assisted carbon coating strategy for improved electrochemical LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathodes
Composition_Formula: LMFP/C: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with conventional glucose-derived carbon coating (control, no iron oxalate)
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis (240 C, 4 h) followed by glucose coating and calcination at 650 C, without the iron oxalate catalyst
Remarks: Uncatalysed control. Discharge capacities 150.4 / 138.9 / 128.4 / 85.9 / 59.0 mAh/g at 0.2 / 0.5 / 1 / 5 / 10C. The two materials are close at low rate but diverge sharply above 1C. Carbon layers are thick and non-uniform, varying between 4.1 and 5.7 nm, with some carbon films stretching away from the particles and contributing nothing electrochemically; Raman IG/ID = 1.11. Rct 78.67 ohm, more than twice the iron-catalysed sample (Warburg factor 43.07, Rs 8.80 ohm).

Paper_Title: Iron-assisted carbon coating strategy for improved electrochemical LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathodes
Composition_Formula: LMFP/Fe/C: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with iron-catalysed graphitised carbon coating
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis followed by sequential iron oxalate and glucose coating, then calcination at 650 C in N2
Remarks: Cycling at the demanding 10C rate for 60 cycles retains 78.6% of capacity, twice the control value. The improvement is credited to the highly graphitised carbon layer reducing the number of lithium ions stranded in the carbon during cycling, thereby maintaining the lithium transference number. Coulombic efficiency also fades far more slowly with increasing rate than for the control.

Paper_Title: Iron-assisted carbon coating strategy for improved electrochemical LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 cathodes
Composition_Formula: LMFP/C: LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 with conventional glucose-derived carbon coating (control)
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal synthesis followed by glucose coating and calcination at 650 C in N2 (no iron oxalate)
Remarks: Cycling at 10C for 60 cycles retains only 39.1% of capacity, against 78.6% for the iron-catalysed sample - the clearest demonstration in the paper that coating quality rather than bulk composition governs high-rate durability.

Paper_Title: Beneficial effect of incorporating particle nanocrystalline and V3+ doping into high-energy-density LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Mechanical liquid-phase activation (planetary ball mill, 400 rpm, 4 h, ball:material 15:1, 500 g/L solids) followed by two-stage carbothermal reduction
Remarks: Undoped baseline. 138 mAh/g at 0.1C; after 100 cycles at 1C it retains 87.3 mAh/g at 84.4% retention. The relatively inert Li+ transport structure causes large charge/discharge polarisation and side reactions including formation of electrochemically inactive heterophases and manganese dissolution. Lattice a = 10.42343, b = 6.08378, c = 4.73586 A, Rw = 2.612%.

Paper_Title: Beneficial effect of incorporating particle nanocrystalline and V3+ doping into high-energy-density LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Mechanical liquid-phase activation (planetary ball mill, 400 rpm, 4 h, ball:material 15:1, 500 g/L solids) followed by two-stage carbothermal reduction
Remarks: Intermediate doping level. 145.3 mAh/g at 0.1C, between the undoped baseline and the 1 at.% optimum. Lattice parameters for this composition are not tabulated.

Paper_Title: Beneficial effect of incorporating particle nanocrystalline and V3+ doping into high-energy-density LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Mechanical liquid-phase activation (planetary ball mill, 400 rpm, 4 h, ball:material 15:1, 500 g/L solids) followed by two-stage carbothermal reduction
Remarks: Optimum composition and the headline result of the paper. Rate capability 155.4 / 149.2 / 142.6 / 132.3 / 115.9 mAh/g at 0.1 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 / 5.0C; retains 131.1 mAh/g after 100 cycles at 1C at 93.4% retention. At this level V3+ dissolves fully into the LiMnPO4 lattice as a uniform solid solution - no Li3V2(PO4)3 diffraction peaks and a single 0.373 nm (011) lattice fringe in HRTEM under the carbon coating. Charge-transfer resistance is less than half the undoped value and the charging Li+ diffusion coefficient is more than three times higher. Lattice a = 10.41365, b = 6.07772, c = 4.73326 A, Rw = 2.340%; vanadium addition contracts the cell volume.

Paper_Title: Beneficial effect of incorporating particle nanocrystalline and V3+ doping into high-energy-density LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Mechanical liquid-phase activation (planetary ball mill, 400 rpm, 4 h, ball:material 15:1, 500 g/L solids) followed by two-stage carbothermal reduction
Remarks: 152.8 mAh/g at 0.1C, marginally below the 1 at.% optimum. Still shows no NASICON Li3V2(PO4)3 diffraction peaks, so roughly 2 at.% is the upper solubility limit of V3+ in the olivine lattice under these synthesis conditions; XPS nevertheless finds vanadium enriched at the particle surface relative to the nominal doping level. Lattice a = 10.40819, b = 6.07455, c = 4.73519 A, Rw = 2.490%.

Paper_Title: Beneficial effect of incorporating particle nanocrystalline and V3+ doping into high-energy-density LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Mechanical liquid-phase activation (planetary ball mill, 400 rpm, 4 h, ball:material 15:1, 500 g/L solids) followed by two-stage carbothermal reduction
Remarks: Above the solubility limit: Li3V2(PO4)3 (LVP) diffraction peaks are now detectable, with a refined LVP fraction of 0.129. XPS depth profiling on this sample is the key evidence for surface enrichment - relative V content is 54.1% at the outermost surface, ten times the ideal uniform-doping value, and falls rapidly with etching depth while Mn2+ and Fe2+ rise, showing that excess vanadium forms a V-rich surface coating rather than doping the bulk. Lattice a = 10.40861, b = 6.07384, c = 4.73435 A, Rw = 2.557%. Electrochemical data are not separately tabulated for this composition.

Paper_Title: Beneficial effect of incorporating particle nanocrystalline and V3+ doping into high-energy-density LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Mechanical liquid-phase activation (planetary ball mill, 400 rpm, 4 h, ball:material 15:1, 500 g/L solids) followed by two-stage carbothermal reduction
Remarks: Smallest cell volume of the series (refined LVP fraction 0.202), consistent with the trend that all of a, b and V fall as vanadium addition increases up to 10 at.%. Lattice a = 10.4048, b = 6.06893, c = 4.73346 A, Rw = 2.525%. Electrochemical data are not separately tabulated for this composition.

Paper_Title: Beneficial effect of incorporating particle nanocrystalline and V3+ doping into high-energy-density LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 for lithium-ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Mechanical liquid-phase activation (planetary ball mill, 400 rpm, 4 h, ball:material 15:1, 500 g/L solids) followed by two-stage carbothermal reduction
Remarks: Over-doped and worse than the undoped baseline on every metric: 128.1 mAh/g at 0.1C and only 42.1 mAh/g remaining after 100 cycles at 1C, a retention of 53.3%. Abundant LVP impurity (refined fraction 0.400) binds to the LMFP and degrades the crystallinity and lattice regularity of both phases; HRTEM resolves two distinct lattices, 0.259 nm (121) olivine LiMnPO4 and 0.2492 nm (2 0 -4) NASICON Li3V2(PO4)3, confirmed by FFT as Pnma and P21/n domains. Lattice a = 10.41358, b = 6.07834, c = 4.7376 A, Rw = 3.344%. Note the two-step reaction confirmed by XPS: V(V) in V2O5 is reduced to V(III) while metallic Mn0 and Fe0 are oxidised to Mn(II) and Fe(II) during activation-assisted carbothermal reduction.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Hydrothermal (urea as N source)
Remarks: 180 mg GO dispersed in 360 mL deionized water with 2 h ultrasonication, 3.6 g urea added and stirred 1 h, then heated at 160 C for 3 h in a 200 mL Teflon-lined autoclave; GO is N-doped by urea, reduced and self-assembled into three-dimensional structures via pi-pi conjugation; washed to neutral and freeze-dried overnight. Four-probe electronic conductivity 254.06 S/cm, higher than plain rGO (165.87 S/cm) and far above amorphous carbon (0.44 S/cm), confirming N-doping enhances rGO conductivity.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal + carbonization
Remarks: Control synthesised without any graphene: stoichiometric MnSO4.H2O, FeSO4.7H2O, H3PO4 (85 wt%) and ascorbic acid in ethylene glycol-water, with LiOH.H2O added dropwise at a Li:Mn/Fe:P molar ratio of 3:1:1, stirred 20 min under N2 and heated at 240 C for 4 h; the precipitate was washed, dried at 45 C for 12 h, mixed with glucose, heated at 350 C for 3 h and carbonized at 650 C under N2. Carbon content 7 wt% (amorphous only). XRD matches the olivine LiMnPO4 pattern with no impurity peaks; the carbon phase is barely visible, indicating the glucose-derived residual carbon is amorphous.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal + carbonization
Remarks: Prepared by the identical route with 2 wt% plain (non-N-doped) rGO added. Total carbon content 9 wt% (7% amorphous carbon plus 2 wt% rGO). XRD shows sharp diffraction peaks with no impurity phase, indicating rGO does not affect the LiMnPO4 crystal structure; rGO diffraction peaks are not observed owing to its low content.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal + carbonization
Remarks: Prepared by the identical route with the N-rGO powder (2 wt% of the theoretical LMFP weight) pre-sonicated in water and dispersed into the reaction mixture. Total carbon content 9 wt% (7% amorphous carbon plus 2 wt% N-rGO). XRD shows sharp peaks matching the olivine phase with no impurity peaks, so N-rGO does not disturb the crystal structure.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal + carbonization
Remarks: Raman shows the D band at about 1348 cm-1 (disorders/defects in carbon) and the G band at about 1600 cm-1 (graphitic carbon), with an intensity ratio ID/IG of 0.853.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries

Remarks: Raman intensity ratio ID/IG = 0.899, higher than the graphene-free control.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal + carbonization
Remarks: Raman intensity ratio ID/IG = 0.910, the highest of the three samples, indicating more defects after N-doping, consistent with previous reports on N-doped graphitic materials.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal + carbonization
Remarks: SEM shows uniform rod-like particles of around 300 nm in length with relatively uniform distribution and no agglomeration.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal + carbonization
Remarks: LMFP particles of smaller size grown on the N-rGO surface; TEM confirms rod-like particles of 200-300 nm consistent with SEM (the average size field records the midpoint of that range). Addition of rGO or N-rGO does not change the rod-like habit but partly limits crystal growth. HRTEM shows the LMFP tightly coated by a thin amorphous carbon layer about 2 nm thick through which Li+ can easily pass. Profiting from increased wettability from nitrogen-containing functional groups, the contact between N-rGO and LMFP is closer and more uniform than between plain rGO and LMFP.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal + carbonization
Remarks: Full XPS spectrum shows binding energies of 60.62 eV (Li 1s), 139.51 eV (P 2p), 298.62 eV (C 1s), 410.62 eV (N 1s), 539.22 eV (O 1s), 660.62 eV (Mn 2p) and 740.62 eV (Fe 2p). O 1s deconvolutes into four peaks at 530.9, 531.6, 532.1 and 533.4 eV for O-P, O-C, O=C and O-C=O. N 1s contains pyridinic N at 398.5 eV, pyrrolic N at 400.4 eV and graphitic N at 401.4 eV; graphitic N has one more electron than carbon, enhancing the electrical conductivity of N-rGO. C 1s consists of five peaks at 284.8, 285.8, 286.7, 287.9 and 289.8 eV for C-C, C-N, C-O, C=O and O-C=O, the C-N bond confirming formation of N-rGO.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
Synthesis_Method: Solvothermal + carbonization
Remarks: Initial discharge capacity of 156.7 mAh/g at 0.2 C between 2.0 and 4.6 V, the highest of the three samples. Two voltage plateaus around 3.6 V and 4.1 V correspond to the Fe2+/Fe3+ and Mn2+/Mn3+ redox reactions; an additional unexpected plateau around 3.3 V is attributed by the authors to external factors such as electrolyte or battery-system instability. The charge-discharge voltage interval is 0.165 V, much lower than the other two samples, indicating the smallest polarization.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries

Remarks: Initial discharge capacity of 152 mAh/g at 0.2 C with a charge-discharge voltage interval of 0.238 V.

Remarks: Initial discharge capacity of 147.1 mAh/g at 0.2 C with a charge-discharge voltage interval of 0.236 V.

Paper_Title: Heterogeneous carbon/N-doped reduced graphene oxide wrapping LiMn0.8Fe0.2PO4 composite for higher performance of lithium ion batteries
